title.zh: 卷八十一 志第三十一: 選舉一
title.raw: 卷八十一 志第三十一: 選舉一 Volume 81 Treatises 34: Selection of Officials 1

sentences.zh: 選舉一

translations.literal: Selection of Officials 1
translations.idiomatic: Selection of Officials 1

sentences.zh: 選舉之法尚矣。

translations.literal: The methods of official selection are of long standing.
translations.idiomatic: The methods by which officials are chosen are ancient indeed.

sentences.zh: 成周庠序學校，以鄉三物教萬民而賓興之，舉於鄉，升於司徒、司馬論定，而後官之。

translations.literal: In the perfected Zhou, the schools of the state and the village taught the myriad people with the three village teachings and advanced them as guests; they were selected in the village, promoted to the Minister of Education and the Minister of War for deliberation and determination, and only then given office.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhou of King Cheng, state and village schools taught the people through the three village norms and advanced the worthy as guests. Candidates were chosen in the village, sent up to the ministers of education and war for review, and only then appointed to office.

sentences.zh: 兩漢有賢良方正、孝弟力田等科，或奉對詔策，事猶近古。

translations.literal: The two Han dynasties had categories such as Worthy and Upright and Filial and Frugal in Farming, and some presented responses to imperial edicts and policy questions; the practice still resembled antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Under the two Han dynasties there were categories such as Worthy and Upright and Filial and Frugal in Farming, and candidates sometimes answered imperial questions in person—practices that still bore some resemblance to antiquity.

sentences.zh: 隋、唐有秀才、明經、進士、明法、明算等科，或兼用詩賦，士始有棄本而逐末者。

translations.literal: Sui and Tang had categories such as Cultivated Talent, Understanding the Classics, Presented Scholar, Understanding Law, and Understanding Calculation; sometimes poetry and rhapsody were also used, and scholars began to abandon the root and pursue the branch.
translations.idiomatic: Sui and Tang established categories such as Cultivated Talent, Understanding the Classics, Presented Scholar, Understanding Law, and Understanding Calculation, and sometimes added poetry and rhapsody as well. Scholars began to abandon fundamentals and chase ornament.

sentences.zh: 宋大興文治，專尚科目，雖當時得人為盛，而其弊遂至文體卑弱，士習委靡，識者病焉。

translations.literal: Song greatly promoted literary governance and relied exclusively on examination categories; although men of talent were abundant at the time, the abuse eventually led to a debased literary style and a languid scholarly habit, which thoughtful men deplored.
translations.idiomatic: The Song greatly promoted literary governance and relied almost entirely on the examination system. For a time it produced many able men, but in time the style of writing grew feeble and scholarly habits grew slack—failings that thoughtful observers lamented.

sentences.zh: 遼、金居北方，俗尚弓馬，遼景宗、道宗亦行貢試，金太宗、世宗屢辟科場，亦粗稱得士。

translations.literal: Liao and Jin dwelt in the north and their custom honored bow and horse; Liao's Emperor Jingzong and Daozong also held tribute examinations, and Jin's Emperor Taizong and Shizong repeatedly opened examination grounds, and they too could be said in rough measure to have obtained men of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Liao and Jin ruled the north, where the custom favored bow and horse. Even so, Liao's Emperor Jingzong and Daozong held tribute examinations, and Jin's Emperor Taizong and Shizong opened the examination fields many times; they too could be said, in a rough way, to have secured able men.

sentences.zh: 元初，太宗始得中原，輒用耶律楚材言，以科舉選士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuan, when Emperor Taizong first obtained the Central Plains, he promptly adopted Yelü Chucai's advice and used the civil examination to select scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty, as soon as Emperor Taizong gained the Central Plains, he took Yelü Chucai's advice and used the civil examination to select scholars.

sentences.zh: 世祖既定天下，王鶚獻計，許衡立法，事未果行。

translations.literal: After Emperor Shizu had settled the realm, Wang E offered plans and Xu Heng drafted laws, but the matter in the end was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Shizu had settled the realm, Wang E offered plans and Xu Heng drafted regulations, but the reforms were never fully implemented.

sentences.zh: 至仁宗延祐間，始斟酌舊制而行之，取士以德行為本，試藝以經術為先，士褒然舉首應上所求者，皆彬彬輩出矣。

translations.literal: By Emperor Renzong's Yanyou era, the old system was at last weighed and put into practice: scholars were taken on the basis of virtue and conduct, and tested arts with classical learning foremost; those who respectfully raised their heads to answer what the ruler sought all came forth in refined succession.
translations.idiomatic: Not until Emperor Renzong's Yanyou reign did the court weigh the old rules and put them into practice, taking scholars on the basis of virtue and testing them with classical learning first. Men who answered the throne's call came forward in refined succession.

sentences.zh: 然當時仕進有多岐，銓衡無定制，其出身於學校者，有國子監學，有蒙古字學、回回國學，有醫學，有陰陽學。

translations.literal: Yet at that time advancement into office had many branches and assessment had no fixed standard. Those who came from schools included the Directorate of Education, Mongol Script School, Hui Nationality School, Medical School, and Yin-Yang School.
translations.idiomatic: Yet advancement into office had many paths and assessment had no single standard. School graduates might come from the Directorate of Education, the Mongol Script School, the Hui Nationality School, medical schools, or yin-yang schools.

sentences.zh: 其策名於薦舉者，有遺逸，有茂異，有求言，有進書，有童子。

translations.literal: Those who gained fame through recommendation included Recluse Worthies, Outstanding Talents, Requests for Advice, Presentation of Books, and Child Prodigies.
translations.idiomatic: Those who gained office through recommendation included recluses of outstanding merit, men of exceptional talent, petitioners offering counsel, presenters of books, and child prodigies.

sentences.zh: 其出於宿衛、勛臣之家者，待以不次。

translations.literal: Those who came from the households of palace guards and meritorious ministers were treated with extraordinary promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Those from the households of palace guards and meritorious ministers were promoted out of regular order.

sentences.zh: 其用於宣徽、中政之屬者，重為內官。

translations.literal: Those employed in the offices of the Xuanwei and Central Administration were heavily weighted as inner officials.
translations.idiomatic: Those who served in the Xuanwei and Central Administration bureaus were treated as weighty inner-court officials.

sentences.zh: 又蔭敘有循常之格，而超擢有選用之科。

translations.literal: Moreover, for hereditary privilege there were regular grades, while for extraordinary promotion there were selection categories.
translations.idiomatic: Hereditary privilege followed regular grades, while extraordinary promotion had its own selection categories.

sentences.zh: 由直省、侍儀等入官者，亦名清望。

translations.literal: Those who entered office through the Direct Secretariat, Ceremonial Attendants, and the like were also called positions of clear reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Those who entered office through the Direct Secretariat, Ceremonial Attendants, and similar posts were also counted among posts of clear reputation.

sentences.zh: 以倉庾、賦稅任事者，例視冗職。

translations.literal: Those charged with granaries and tax collection were routinely regarded as superfluous posts.
translations.idiomatic: Posts charged with granaries and tax collection were routinely treated as low-status routine work.

sentences.zh: 捕盜者以功敘，入粟者以貲進，至工匠皆入班資，而輿隸亦躋流品。

translations.literal: Bandit-catchers were ranked by merit, grain donors advanced by wealth, and even artisans entered the roster of grades; runners and clerks also ascended into the ranked ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit-catchers advanced by merit, grain donors by wealth, and even artisans entered the official roster; runners and clerks too could rise into the ranked service.

sentences.zh: 諸王、公主，寵以投下，俾之保任。

translations.literal: Princes and princesses were favored with appanages and made to guarantee appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and princesses were favored with appanages and empowered to guarantee appointments.

sentences.zh: 遠夷、外僥，授以長官，俾之世襲。

translations.literal: Distant barbarians and outer border peoples were granted chief posts and made to inherit them in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Distant peoples and border communities were given chief posts to hold in hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 凡若此類，殆所謂吏道雜而多端者歟！

translations.literal: All such cases are perhaps what is called the official way being mixed and many-branched!
translations.idiomatic: Cases such as these are precisely what people mean when they say the paths of officialdom were tangled and manifold.

sentences.zh: 矧夫儒有歲貢之名，吏有補用之法，曰掾史、令史，曰書寫、銓寫，曰書吏、典吏，所設之名，未易枚舉，曰省、臺、院、部，曰路、府、州、縣，所入之途，難以指計。

translations.literal: Moreover, Confucians had the name of annual tribute, clerks had methods of supplementary appointment—called aide clerks and order clerks, called copyists and selection copyists, called document clerks and registry clerks; the titles established are not easy to enumerate one by one. From Secretariat, Censorate, Court, and Ministry to Circuit, Prefecture, Subprefecture, and District, the paths of entry are hard to count by pointing.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Confucians had annual tribute posts and clerks had supplementary appointment routes—aide clerks, order clerks, copyists, selection copyists, document clerks, registry clerks, and more titles than one can easily list. From secretariats, censorates, courts, and ministries down to circuits, prefectures, subprefectures, and districts, the paths into office were beyond easy reckoning.

sentences.zh: 雖名卿大夫，亦往往由是躋要官，受顯爵；

translations.literal: Even those called high ministers and grandees often by this means ascended to important offices and received eminent ranks;
translations.idiomatic: Even men who bore the titles of high minister or grandee often rose to important posts and received eminent ranks by these routes;

sentences.zh: 而刀筆下吏，遂致竊權勢，舞文法矣。

translations.literal: while brush-and-knife subordinate clerks thereby came to usurp power and authority and manipulate the written law.
translations.idiomatic: while lowly clerks who wielded the brush came to seize power and twist the written law.

sentences.zh: 故其銓選之備，考核之精，曰隨朝、外任，曰省選、部選，曰文官、武官，曰考數，曰資格，一毫不可越。

translations.literal: Therefore its provisions for selection and assessment were complete and its scrutiny precise: called attendance at court and service outside, provincial selection and ministry selection, civil officials and military officials, examination counts and qualifications—not a hair's breadth could be overstepped.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly its rules for selection and assessment were elaborate and exact—court service and outside appointment, provincial selection and ministry selection, civil and military posts, examination counts and qualifications—and not a single rule could be crossed.

sentences.zh: 而或援例，或借資，或優升，或回降，其縱情破律，以公濟私，非至明者不能察焉。

translations.literal: Yet some invoked precedents, some borrowed qualifications, some were promoted preferentially, some were demoted in reversal; those who indulged their feelings and broke the statutes, using public office to advance private ends—only the most perceptive could detect them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet some invoked precedents, some borrowed seniority, some won preferential promotion, and some were sent down in rank. Those who bent the rules to serve private ends under cover of public business could be detected only by the sharpest observers.

sentences.zh: 是皆文繁吏弊之所致也。

translations.literal: All these were caused by prolix documents and official abuse.
translations.idiomatic: All of this sprang from prolix paperwork and the abuses of clerical government.

sentences.zh: 今采摭舊編，載於簡牘，或詳或略，絳分類聚，殆有不勝其紀述者，姑存一代之制，作《選舉志》。

translations.literal: Now gathering from old compilations and recording them on bamboo slips, some in detail and some in summary, sorting and grouping them in red, there are almost more than can be fully described; for the present the institutions of one dynasty are preserved in making the "Treatise on Selection of Officials."
translations.idiomatic: The present compilation draws on older records, setting them down in full or in summary and arranging them by category—almost too much to recount in full. For now we preserve the institutions of the dynasty in this Treatise on Selection of Officials.

sentences.zh: ○科目

translations.literal: ○ Examination Categories
translations.idiomatic: Examination Categories

sentences.zh: 太宗始取中原，中書令耶律楚材請用儒術選士，從之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong first took the Central Plains, Chief Minister Yelü Chucai requested using Confucian learning to select scholars, and the emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong first took the Central Plains, Chief Minister Yelü Chucai asked that scholars be chosen through Confucian learning, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 九年秋八月，下詔命斷事官術忽<角┦>與山西東路課稅所長官劉中，歷諸路考試。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, autumn, eighth month, an edict was issued ordering the judicial officer Shuhudai and Liu Zhong, chief of the Shanxi Eastern Circuit Tax Office, to conduct examinations throughout the circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn in the ninth year, an edict ordered the judicial officer Shuhudai and Liu Zhong, head of the Shanxi Eastern Circuit tax office, to hold examinations throughout the circuits.

sentences.zh: 以論及經義、詞賦分為三科，作三日程，專治一科，能兼者聽，但以不失文義為中選。

translations.literal: Discourse, classical meaning, and lyric rhapsody were divided into three categories, with a three-day schedule; each candidate specialized in one category, though those able to combine were permitted, but selection depended only on not failing the literary meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates were tested in discourse, classical exegesis, and lyric composition, divided into three categories over three days. Each was to specialize in one subject, though those able to combine subjects were allowed; selection depended on sound understanding of the texts.

sentences.zh: 其中選者，復其賦役，令與各處長官同署公事，得東平楊奐等凡若干人，皆一時名士，而當世或以為非便，事復中止。

translations.literal: Those selected had their tax and corvée duties restored and were ordered to sign public business together with local chiefs; among those obtained were Yang Huan of Dongping and several others in all, all famous scholars of the time, but contemporaries regarded it as inconvenient, and the matter again ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Those who passed had their tax and corvée obligations restored and were ordered to handle public business alongside local chiefs. Among those chosen were Yang Huan of Dongping and several others, all celebrated scholars of the day, but many contemporaries found the arrangement impractical, and the program was halted again.

sentences.zh: 世祖至元初年，有旨命丞相史天澤絳具當行大事，嘗及科舉，而未果行。

translations.literal: In the early years of Emperor Shizu's Zhiyuan reign, there was an order commanding Chancellor Shi Tianze to compile in detail the great matters that should be undertaken; the civil examination was once included, but in the end was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Shizu's Zhiyuan reign, the emperor ordered Chancellor Shi Tianze to compile in detail the major reforms that should be undertaken. The civil examination was discussed, but never implemented.

sentences.zh: 四年九月，翰林學士承旨王鶚等，請行選舉法，遠述周制，次及漢、隋、唐取士科目，近舉遼、金選舉用人，與本朝太宗得人之效，以為：「貢舉法廢，士無入仕之階，或習刀筆以為吏胥，或執仆役以事官僚，或作技巧販鬻以為工匠商賈。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, ninth month, Hanlin Academician Wang E and others requested implementing the selection law, describing the Zhou system from afar, then Han, Sui, and Tang categories for taking scholars, and citing recent Liao and Jin selection and employment, together with the effect of Emperor Taizong of our dynasty in obtaining men, stating: "With the tribute-examination law abandoned, scholars have no ladder into office; some study brush and knife to become clerk assistants, some perform menial service to attend on bureaucrats, some practice crafts and trade to become artisans and merchants.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year, Hanlin Academician Wang E and others asked that the selection law be implemented. They reviewed the Zhou system, then Han, Sui, and Tang methods of recruitment, and cited Liao and Jin practice together with the success of our Taizong in securing talent. They argued: "With the tribute-examination system abandoned, scholars have no path into office. Some learn clerical skills to become aides, some serve as attendants to officials, and some turn to crafts and trade as artisans or merchants.

sentences.zh: 以今論之，惟科舉取士，最為切務，矧先朝故典，尤宜追述。」

translations.literal: Speaking of the present, only the civil examination for selecting scholars is the most urgent task; moreover the former dynasty's old statutes should especially be followed and restored."
translations.idiomatic: For the present, nothing is more urgent than restoring the civil examination, and the precedents of the former dynasty should especially be revived."

sentences.zh: 奏上，帝曰：「此良法也，其行之。」

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor said: "This is a good law; carry it out."
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, the emperor said, "This is sound policy. Put it into practice."

sentences.zh: 中書左三部與翰林學士議立程式，又請：「依前代立國學，選蒙古人諸職官子孫百人，專命師儒教習經書，俟其藝成，然後試用，庶幾勛舊之家，人材輩出，以備超擢。」

translations.literal: The Left Three Departments of the Secretariat and Hanlin academicians discussed establishing procedures, and further requested: "Following former dynasties, establish the National University, select one hundred descendants of Mongol officials, specially appoint teachers to instruct them in the classics, and after their arts are complete then try them in service, so that from meritorious old households talents may emerge in succession to supply extraordinary promotion."
translations.idiomatic: The Left Three Departments of the Secretariat and the Hanlin academicians drafted procedures and further asked that, following earlier dynasties, a National University be established. One hundred descendants of Mongol officials were to be chosen and taught the classics by appointed teachers; only after they had mastered their studies were they to be tried in office, so that meritorious households might produce talent for extraordinary promotion."

sentences.zh: 十一年十一月，裕宗在東宮時，省臣復啟，謂「去年奉旨行科舉，今將翰林老臣等所議程式以聞」。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, eleventh month, when Crown Prince Yuzong was in the Eastern Palace, provincial ministers again reported, saying, "Last year we received the order to carry out the civil examination; now we report the procedures discussed by the old Hanlin ministers and others."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the eleventh year, while Crown Prince Yuzong was in the Eastern Palace, provincial ministers reported again that, having received orders the previous year to implement the civil examination, they now submitted the procedures drafted by senior Hanlin scholars.

sentences.zh: 奉令旨，準蒙古進士科及漢人進士科，參酌時宜，以立制度，事未施行。

translations.literal: Receiving the command edict, they approved the Mongol Presented Scholar category and the Han Presented Scholar category, weighed them against the needs of the time to establish the system, but the matter was not yet implemented.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial command they approved Mongol and Han Presented Scholar categories and drafted a system suited to the times, but the reforms were still not implemented.

sentences.zh: 至二十一年九月，丞相火魯火孫與留夢炎等言，十一月中書省臣奏，皆以為天下習儒者少，而由刀筆吏得官者多。

translations.literal: By the twenty-first year, ninth month, Chancellor Huoluohusun and Liu Mengyan and others spoke; in the eleventh month Secretariat ministers memorialized, all holding that those in the realm who studied Confucian learning were few, while those who obtained office through brush-and-knife clerks were many.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the twenty-first year, Chancellor Huoluohusun and Liu Mengyan and others spoke on the matter. In the eleventh month Secretariat ministers memorialized that few men in the realm studied Confucian learning, while many gained office through clerical service.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「將若之何？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What is to be done about it?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "What is to be done about it?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「惟貢舉取士為便。

translations.literal: They replied: "Only tribute-examination selection of scholars is convenient.
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "The tribute-examination system is the best remedy.

sentences.zh: 凡蒙古之士及儒吏、陰陽、醫術，皆令試舉，則用心為學矣。」

translations.literal: All Mongol scholars, as well as Confucian clerks, yin-yang specialists, and medical practitioners, should be ordered to take the examination trial; then they will apply their minds to learning."
translations.idiomatic: If Mongol scholars, Confucian clerks, yin-yang specialists, and medical practitioners were all required to sit for examinations, they would devote themselves to study."

sentences.zh: 帝可其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor approved their memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 繼而許衡亦議學校科舉之法，罷詩賦，重經學，定為新制。

translations.literal: Thereafter Xu Heng also discussed the methods of schools and the civil examination, abolishing poetry and rhapsody, emphasizing classical learning, and fixing a new system.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Heng then proposed reforms to schools and the civil examination, abolishing poetry and rhapsody, emphasizing classical learning, and establishing a new system.

sentences.zh: 事雖未及行，而選舉之制已立。

translations.literal: Although the matter had not yet been carried out, the system of selection was already established.
translations.idiomatic: Although the reforms had not yet been implemented, the framework for official selection was already in place.

sentences.zh: 至仁宗皇慶二年十月，中書省臣奏：「科舉事，世祖、裕宗累嘗命行，成宗、武宗尋亦有旨，今不以聞，恐或有沮其事者。

translations.literal: By Emperor Renzong's Huangqing second year, tenth month, Secretariat ministers memorialized: "Regarding the civil examination, Emperor Shizu and Crown Prince Yuzong repeatedly ordered its implementation; Emperor Chengzong and Emperor Wuzong soon afterward also issued edicts. If it is not now reported, I fear there may be those who obstruct the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the second year of Emperor Renzong's Huangqing reign, Secretariat ministers memorialized: "As for the civil examination, Emperor Shizu and Crown Prince Yuzong repeatedly ordered its implementation, and Emperors Chengzong and Wuzong soon issued further edicts. If we do not report progress now, someone may obstruct the project.

sentences.zh: 夫取士之法，經學實修己治人之道，詞賦乃摛章繪句之學，自隋、唐以來，取人專尚詞賦，故士習浮華。

translations.literal: The method of taking scholars: classical learning is truly the Way of cultivating the self and governing others; lyric rhapsody is the learning of composing chapters and painting phrases. Since Sui and Tang, selection has exclusively honored lyric rhapsody, and therefore scholarly habit has become showy and superficial.
translations.idiomatic: The proper way to recruit officials is through classical learning, which cultivates the self and governs others. Lyric composition is merely the art of polished phrasing. Since Sui and Tang, recruitment has favored poetry and rhapsody, and scholarly habits have grown showy and hollow.

sentences.zh: 今臣等所擬將律賦省題詩小義皆不用，專立德行明經科，以此取士，庶可得人。」

translations.literal: What your ministers now propose is to set aside regulated rhapsody, provincial topic poetry, and minor meanings entirely, and establish only the categories of Virtue and Conduct and Understanding the Classics; by this means to take scholars, we may hope to obtain men."
translations.idiomatic: We propose to abolish regulated rhapsody, provincial-topic poetry, and minor exegetical questions, and to establish only the categories of Virtue and Conduct and Understanding the Classics. By this means we may hope to secure true talent."

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乃下詔曰：「惟我祖宗以神武定天下，世祖皇帝設官分職，徵用儒雅，崇學校為育材之地，議科舉為取士之方，規模宏遠矣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, an edict was then issued, saying: "Our ancestors by divine martial prowess settled the realm. Emperor Shizu established offices and divided duties, recruited the refined and elegant, honored schools as the ground for nurturing talent, and discussed the civil examination as the method for taking scholars—the design was vast and far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the emperor issued an edict: "Our ancestors settled the realm by divine martial prowess. Emperor Shizu established offices and divided duties, recruited cultivated scholars, honored schools as places to nurture talent, and planned the civil examination as the means to recruit officials—a design of vast scope.

sentences.zh: 朕以眇躬，獲承丕祚，繼誌述事，祖訓是式。

translations.literal: I, with my slight person, have received the great succession, continuing the will and carrying on the affairs, taking ancestral instruction as my model.
translations.idiomatic: I, in my slight person, have received the great succession and now carry on the work of my forebears, taking their instruction as my model.

sentences.zh: 若稽三代以來，取士各有科目，要其本末，舉人宜以德行為首，試藝則以經術為先，詞章次之。

translations.literal: If we examine from the Three Dynasties onward, each had its categories for taking scholars; in essentials and fundamentals, candidates should take virtue and conduct first, and in testing arts classical learning should come first, literary composition second.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back from the Three Dynasties, each age had its own recruitment categories. In essentials, candidates should be judged first on virtue and conduct, and in testing, classical learning should come first and literary composition second.

sentences.zh: 浮華過實，朕所不取。

translations.literal: Showiness exceeding substance—I do not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Showiness without substance is what I reject.

sentences.zh: 爰命中書，參酌古今，定其條制。

translations.literal: Therefore I command the Secretariat to weigh past and present and fix its regulations.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore command the Secretariat to weigh past and present practice and fix the regulations.

sentences.zh: 其以皇慶三年八月，天下郡縣，興其賢者能者，充賦有司，次年二月會試京師，中選者朕將親策焉。

translations.literal: Let it be in Huangqing third year, eighth month, that throughout the realm's commanderies and districts the worthy and able are raised, presented as tribute to the responsible offices; in the second year, second month, they shall assemble for examination in the capital, and those selected I shall personally examine by policy question.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year of Huangqing, commanderies and districts throughout the realm shall present their worthy and able men to the responsible offices. In the second month of the following year they shall assemble in the capital for examination, and those who pass I shall examine in person.

sentences.zh: 具合行事宜於後：科場，每三歲一次開試。

translations.literal: The matters to be jointly carried out are set forth below: examination grounds shall open once every three years.
translations.idiomatic: The regulations to be carried out are as follows. Examinations shall be held once every three years.

sentences.zh: 舉人從本貫官司於諸色戶內推舉，年及二十五以上，鄉黨稱其孝悌，朋友服其信義，經明行修之士，結罪保舉，以禮敦遣，資諸路府。

translations.literal: Candidates shall be recommended from their native place's office among all categories of households; age twenty-five and above; the village and neighborhood praise their filial piety and fraternal duty, friends submit to their faith and righteousness; scholars clear in the classics and cultivated in conduct shall be bound by sworn guarantee and recommended, sent with ceremony, and supplied to the circuit and prefectural offices.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates shall be recommended by the offices of their native place from among all household categories. They must be twenty-five or older, praised in their community for filial piety and fraternal duty, and trusted by friends for faith and integrity. Scholars accomplished in the classics and conduct shall be recommended under sworn guarantee, sent forward with proper ceremony, and dispatched to circuit and prefectural offices.

sentences.zh: 其或徇私濫舉，並應舉而不舉者，監察御史、肅政廉訪司體察究治。

translations.literal: If there is favoritism in recommendation or indiscriminate nomination, or failure to nominate those who ought to be nominated, investigating censors and the Commission for Upholding Justice and Visiting Officials shall investigate and punish.
translations.idiomatic: Where recommendations are made from private favor or where qualified men are passed over, investigating censors and the Commission for Upholding Justice shall investigate and punish offenders.

sentences.zh: 考試程式：蒙古、色目人，第一場經問五絳，《大學》、《論語》、《孟子》、《中庸》內設問，用朱氏章句集註。

translations.literal: Examination procedures: for Mongols and persons of other colors, the first session has five threads of classic questions, with questions set from the Great Learning, Analects, Mencius, and Doctrine of the Mean, using Zhu Xi's collected commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: Examination procedures: For Mongols and persons of other colors, the first session consists of five classic questions drawn from the Great Learning, Analects, Mencius, and Doctrine of the Mean, using Zhu Xi's collected commentaries.

sentences.zh: 其義理精明，文辭典雅者為中選。

translations.literal: Those clear in principle and meaning, and elegant in literary expression, are selected.
translations.idiomatic: Those who show clear understanding of principle and elegant expression shall pass.

sentences.zh: 第二場策一道，以時務出題，限五百字以上。

translations.literal: The second session has one policy question, with topics drawn from current affairs, limited to five hundred characters or more.
translations.idiomatic: The second session is one policy question on current affairs, of no fewer than five hundred characters.

sentences.zh: 漢人、南人，第一場明經經疑二問，《大學》、《論語》、《孟子》、《中庸》內出題，並用朱氏章句集註，復以己意結之，限三百字以上；

translations.literal: For Han people and southern people, the first session has two questions on Understanding the Classics and classic doubts, with topics from the Great Learning, Analects, Mencius, and Doctrine of the Mean, all using Zhu Xi's collected commentaries, and additionally concluding in one's own meaning, limited to three hundred characters or more;
translations.idiomatic: For Han and southern candidates, the first session has two questions on Understanding the Classics and classic difficulties, drawn from the Four Books with Zhu Xi's commentaries, with an additional personal conclusion of no fewer than three hundred characters;

sentences.zh: 經義一道，各治一經，《詩》以朱氏為主，《尚書》以蔡氏為主，《周易》以程氏、朱氏為主，已上三經，兼用古註疏，《春秋》許用《三傳》及胡氏《傳》，《禮記》用古註疏，限五百字以上，不拘格律。

translations.literal: one question on classic meaning, each specializing in one classic: for the Odes Zhu's commentary is primary, for the Documents Cai's is primary, for the Changes Cheng's and Zhu's are primary; for the above three classics ancient commentaries and subcommentaries may also be used; for the Spring and Autumn Annals the Three Commentaries and Master Hu's Commentary are permitted; for the Record of Rites ancient commentaries and subcommentaries are used; limited to five hundred characters or more, not bound by formal rules.
translations.idiomatic: one question on classic exegesis, each candidate specializing in one classic—the Odes chiefly by Zhu, the Documents by Cai, the Changes by Cheng and Zhu, with ancient commentaries also permitted for these three; the Spring and Autumn Annals may use the Three Commentaries and Hu Anguo's commentary; the Record of Rites uses ancient commentaries—no fewer than five hundred characters, without formal constraints.

sentences.zh: 第二場古賦詔誥章表內科一道，古賦詔誥用古體，章表四六，參用古體。

translations.literal: The second session has one category from ancient rhapsody, edict, patent, memorial, and table: ancient rhapsody and edict-patent use ancient style, memorials and tables use parallel prose of four-six, with ancient style also permitted in part.
translations.idiomatic: The second session is one question in ancient rhapsody, edict, patent, memorial, or table—ancient rhapsody and edict-patent in ancient style, memorials and tables in parallel prose, with some use of ancient style permitted.

sentences.zh: 第三場策一道，經史時務內出題，不矜浮藻，惟務直述，限一千字以上成。

translations.literal: The third session has one policy question, with topics from classics, history, and current affairs; do not pride oneself on floating ornament, but only strive for direct statement, limited to one thousand characters or more to complete.
translations.idiomatic: The third session is one policy question drawn from the classics, history, and current affairs. Candidates should not indulge in ornament but write plainly, in no fewer than one thousand characters.

sentences.zh: 蒙古、色目人，願試漢人、南人科目，中選者加一等註授。

translations.literal: Mongols and persons of other colors who wish to take the Han and southern people's categories, if selected, receive appointment notation one grade higher.
translations.idiomatic: Mongols and persons of other colors who choose to sit for the Han and southern examinations, if they pass, receive appointment one grade higher.

sentences.zh: 蒙古、色目人作一榜，漢人、南人作一榜。

translations.literal: Mongols and persons of other colors form one roster, Han people and southern people form one roster.
translations.idiomatic: Mongols and persons of other colors form one roster; Han and southern candidates form another.

sentences.zh: 第一名賜進士及第，從六品，第二名以下及第二甲，皆正七品，第三甲以下，皆正八品，兩榜並同。

translations.literal: First place is granted Presented Scholar with Honors, rank 6b; from second place down and the second class, all rank 7a; third class and below, all rank 8a; both rosters are the same.
translations.idiomatic: First place receives the title Presented Scholar with Honors at rank 6b; from second place through the second class, rank 7a; third class and below, rank 8a—the same for both rosters.

sentences.zh: 所在官司遲誤開試日期，監察御史、肅政廉訪司糾彈治罪。

translations.literal: If local offices delay and miss the examination opening date, investigating censors and the Commission for Upholding Justice shall impeach and punish.
translations.idiomatic: If local offices delay the opening of examinations, investigating censors and the Commission for Upholding Justice shall impeach and punish them.

sentences.zh: 流官子孫蔭敘，並依舊制，願試中選者，優升一等。

translations.literal: For descendants of ranked officials, hereditary privilege follows the old system; those who wish to take the examination and are selected receive preferential promotion of one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants of ranked officials receive hereditary privilege under the old rules; those who choose to sit for the examination and pass are promoted one grade preferentially.

sentences.zh: 在官未入流品，願試者聽。

translations.literal: Those in office who have not entered the ranked grades, if they wish to take the examination, are permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Officials not yet in the ranked grades who wish to sit for the examination are permitted to do so.

sentences.zh: 若中選之人，已有九品以上資級，比附一高，加一等註授；

translations.literal: If those selected already have qualification grades of the ninth rank or above, they are compared to one rank higher and receive appointment notation one grade added;
translations.idiomatic: If a successful candidate already holds qualification of rank nine or above, appointment shall be one grade higher than his present standing;

sentences.zh: 若無品級，止依試例從優銓註。

translations.literal: if without rank grade, appointment follows only the examination precedent with preferential assessment.
translations.idiomatic: if he holds no rank, appointment follows the examination rules with preferential assessment.

sentences.zh: 鄉試處所，並其餘條目，命中書省議行。

translations.literal: The places for provincial examinations and the remaining articles are commanded to the Secretariat for discussion and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The sites for provincial examinations and all remaining provisions are referred to the Secretariat for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 經明行修，庶得真儒之用；

translations.literal: Clear in the classics and cultivated in conduct—we may hope to obtain the use of true Confucians;
translations.idiomatic: May men clear in the classics and cultivated in conduct serve as true Confucian officials;

sentences.zh: 風移俗易，益臻至治之隆。

translations.literal: customs shift and habits change, further reaching the height of utmost governance.
translations.idiomatic: may customs be transformed and governance brought to its fullest height.

sentences.zh: 咨爾多方，體予至意。」

translations.literal: Take counsel, all regions—embody my utmost intent."
translations.idiomatic: Take heed, all regions, and embody my utmost intent."

sentences.zh: 中書省所定條目：

translations.literal: Articles fixed by the Secretariat:
translations.idiomatic: Articles fixed by the Secretariat:

sentences.zh: 鄉試中選者，各給解據、錄連取中科文，行省移咨都省，送禮部，腹裏宣慰司及各路關申禮部，拘該監察御史、廉訪司，依上錄連科文申臺，轉呈都省，以憑照勘。

translations.literal: Those selected in the provincial examination shall each be given credentials of release and a connected record of the examination compositions; the regional secretariat sends consultation to the metropolitan secretariat and forwards to the Ministry of Rites; the metropolitan pacification commissions within the core and each circuit submit to the Ministry of Rites, detaining the relevant investigating censor and visiting official, who according to the above record the connected examination compositions and report to the commission, which forwards to the metropolitan secretariat for verification and inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Those who pass the provincial examination shall each receive credentials and a connected record of their examination papers. The regional secretariat shall consult the metropolitan secretariat and forward the papers to the Ministry of Rites. Pacification commissions in the core region and each circuit shall submit to the Ministry of Rites, with the relevant investigating censor and visiting official recording the papers and reporting to the commission, which forwards them to the metropolitan secretariat for verification.

sentences.zh: 鄉試，八月二十日，蒙古、色目人，試經問五絳；

translations.literal: Provincial examination, twentieth day of the eighth month: Mongols and persons of other colors take the five threads of classic questions;
translations.idiomatic: Provincial examination, twentieth day of the eighth month: Mongols and persons of other colors sit for the five classic questions;

sentences.zh: 漢人、南人，明經經疑二問，經義一道。

translations.literal: Han people and southern people take two questions on Understanding the Classics and classic doubts, and one on classic meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Han and southern candidates take two questions on Understanding the Classics and classic difficulties, and one on classic exegesis.

sentences.zh: 二十三日，蒙古、色目人，試策一道；

translations.literal: Twenty-third day: Mongols and persons of other colors take one policy question;
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-third day: Mongols and persons of other colors take one policy question;

sentences.zh: 漢人、南人，古賦詔誥章表內科一道。

translations.literal: Han people and southern people take one category from ancient rhapsody, edict, patent, memorial, and table.
translations.idiomatic: Han and southern candidates take one question in ancient rhapsody, edict, patent, memorial, or table.

sentences.zh: 二十六日，漢人、南人，試策一道。

translations.literal: Twenty-sixth day: Han people and southern people take one policy question.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-sixth day: Han and southern candidates take one policy question.

sentences.zh: 會試，省部依鄉試例，於次年二月初一日試第一場，初三日第二場，初五日第三場。

translations.literal: Metropolitan examination: the provincial ministries follow the provincial examination precedent, in the second year, second month, first day for the first session, third day for the second session, fifth day for the third session.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan examination: following the provincial model, the ministries hold the first session on the first day of the second month of the following year, the second on the third day, and the third on the fifth.

sentences.zh: 禦試，三月初七日，前期奏委考試官二員、監察御史二員、讀卷官二員，入殿廷考試。

translations.literal: Palace examination, seventh day of the third month: beforehand memorializing appointment of two examination officials, two investigating censors, and two reading officials, to enter the palace hall for examination.
translations.idiomatic: Palace examination, seventh day of the third month: beforehand the court appoints two examination officials, two investigating censors, and two reading officials to conduct the examination in the palace hall.

sentences.zh: 每舉子一名，怯薛歹一人看守。

translations.literal: For each candidate one keshik guard is assigned to watch.
translations.idiomatic: One imperial guard is assigned to watch each candidate.

sentences.zh: 漢人、南人，試策一道，限一千字以上成。

translations.literal: Han people and southern people take one policy question, limited to one thousand characters or more to complete.
translations.idiomatic: Han and southern candidates take one policy question of no fewer than one thousand characters.

sentences.zh: 蒙古、色目人，時務策一道，限五百字以上成。

translations.literal: Mongols and persons of other colors take one policy question on current affairs, limited to five hundred characters or more to complete.
translations.idiomatic: Mongols and persons of other colors take one policy question on current affairs of no fewer than five hundred characters.

sentences.zh: 選考試官，行省與宣慰司及腹裏各路，有行臺及廉訪司去處，與臺憲官一同商議選差。

translations.literal: Selecting examination officials: the regional secretariat, pacification commission, and circuits within the core—in places where there is a regional commission and visiting officials—shall together with commission and censorate officials consult and select appointees.
translations.idiomatic: Examination officials shall be chosen by the regional secretariat, pacification commission, and core circuits, consulting together with regional commission and censorate officials where those offices exist.

sentences.zh: 上都、大都從省部選差在內監察御史、在外廉訪司官一員監試。

translations.literal: At Shangdu and Dadu, the ministries select one investigating censor within and one visiting official without to supervise the examination.
translations.idiomatic: At Shangdu and Dadu the ministries appoint one investigating censor and one visiting official to supervise the examination.

sentences.zh: 每處差考試官、同考試官各一員，並於見任並在閑有德望文學常選官內選差；

translations.literal: At each place one examination official and one associate examination official are appointed, all selected from among incumbent and retired officials of virtue, reputation, literary learning, and regular selection;
translations.idiomatic: Each site shall appoint one chief examiner and one associate examiner, chosen from incumbent or retired officials of reputation and literary accomplishment;

sentences.zh: 封彌官一員、謄錄官一員，選廉幹文資正官充之。

translations.literal: one sealing official and one copying official, chosen from upright, capable civil officials of regular rank to fill the posts.
translations.idiomatic: and one sealing official and one copying official, chosen from upright civil officials of regular rank.

sentences.zh: 凡謄錄試卷並行移文字，皆用朱書，仍須設法關防，毋致容私作弊。

translations.literal: All copied examination papers and transmitted documents shall use red ink, and methods of seal and guard must still be established so as not to allow private favoritism and cheating.
translations.idiomatic: All copied examination papers and official documents shall be written in red ink, with safeguards established to prevent favoritism and cheating.

sentences.zh: 省部會試，都省選委知貢舉、同知貢舉官各一員，考試官四員，監察御史二員，彌封、謄錄、對讀官、監門等官各一員。

translations.literal: For the provincial ministries' metropolitan examination, the metropolitan secretariat selects and appoints one Director of Tribute Presentation, one Associate Director of Tribute Presentation, four examination officials, two investigating censors, and one each of sealing, copying, collation, and gate-guard officials.
translations.idiomatic: For the metropolitan examination the metropolitan secretariat appoints one Director of Tribute Presentation, one Associate Director, four examiners, two investigating censors, and one each of sealing, copying, collation, and gate-guard officials.

sentences.zh: 鄉試，行省一十一：河南，陜西，遼陽，四川，甘肅，雲南，嶺北，征東，江浙，江西，湖廣。

translations.literal: Provincial examinations, eleven regional secretariats: Henan, Shaanxi, Liaoyang, Sichuan, Gansu, Yunnan, Lingbei, Eastern Campaign, Jiang-Zhe, Jiangxi, Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial examinations are held in eleven regional secretariats: Henan, Shaanxi, Liaoyang, Sichuan, Gansu, Yunnan, Lingbei, Eastern Campaign, Jiang-Zhe, Jiangxi, and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 宣慰司二：河東，山東。

translations.literal: Two pacification commissions: Hedong, Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Two pacification commissions: Hedong and Shandong.

sentences.zh: 直隸省部路分四：真定，東平，大都，上都。

translations.literal: The Directorate circuits under the metropolitan ministries are divided into four: Zhending, Dongping, Dadu, and Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Under the metropolitan ministries there are four circuits: Zhending, Dongping, Dadu, and Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 天下選合格者三百人赴會試，於內取中選者一百人，內蒙古、色目、漢人、南人分卷考試，各二十五人，蒙古人取合格者七十五人：大都十五人，上都六人，河東五人，真定等五人，東平等五人。

translations.literal: Throughout the realm three hundred who passed selection went to the metropolitan examination; from within these one hundred were selected. Within this, Mongols, persons of other colors, Han people, and southern people took separate examination rolls, twenty-five each. Mongols who passed selection numbered seventy-five: Dadu fifteen, Shangdu six, Hedong five, Zhending and others five, Dongping and others five.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred qualified candidates from across the realm proceeded to the metropolitan examination, of whom one hundred were selected. Mongols, persons of other colors, Han, and southern candidates sat in separate rolls of twenty-five each. Seventy-five Mongols were to pass: fifteen from Dadu, six from Shangdu, five from Hedong, five from Zhending and related circuits, and five from Dongping and related circuits.

sentences.zh: 山東四人，遼陽五人，河南五人，陜西五人，甘肅三人，嶺北三人，江浙五人，江西三人，湖廣三人，四川一人，雲南一人，征東一人。

translations.literal: Shandong four, Liaoyang five, Henan five, Shaanxi five, Gansu three, Lingbei three, Jiang-Zhe five, Jiangxi three, Huguang three, Sichuan one, Yunnan one, Eastern Campaign one.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong four, Liaoyang five, Henan five, Shaanxi five, Gansu three, Lingbei three, Jiang-Zhe five, Jiangxi three, Huguang three, Sichuan one, Yunnan one, and Eastern Campaign one.

sentences.zh: 色目人取合格者七十五人：大都十人，上都四人，河東四人，東平等四人，山東五人，真定等五人，河南五人，四川三人，甘肅二人，陜西三人，嶺北二人，遼陽二人，雲南二人，征東一人，湖廣七人，江浙一十人，江西六人。

translations.literal: Persons of other colors who passed selection numbered seventy-five: Dadu ten, Shangdu four, Hedong four, Dongping and others four, Shandong five, Zhending and others five, Henan five, Sichuan three, Gansu two, Shaanxi three, Lingbei two, Liaoyang two, Yunnan two, Eastern Campaign one, Huguang seven, Jiang-Zhe ten, Jiangxi six.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-five persons of other colors were to pass: ten from Dadu, four from Shangdu, four from Hedong, four from Dongping and related circuits, five from Shandong, five from Zhending and related circuits, five from Henan, three from Sichuan, two from Gansu, three from Shaanxi, two from Lingbei, two from Liaoyang, two from Yunnan, one from Eastern Campaign, seven from Huguang, ten from Jiang-Zhe, and six from Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 漢人取合格者七十五人：大都一十人，上都四人，真定等十一人，東平等九人，山東七人，河東七人，河南九人，四川五人，雲南二人，甘肅二人，嶺北一人，陜西五人，遼陽二人，征東一人。

translations.literal: Han people who passed selection numbered seventy-five: Dadu ten, Shangdu four, Zhending and others eleven, Dongping and others nine, Shandong seven, Hedong seven, Henan nine, Sichuan five, Yunnan two, Gansu two, Lingbei one, Shaanxi five, Liaoyang two, Eastern Campaign one.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-five Han candidates were to pass: ten from Dadu, four from Shangdu, eleven from Zhending and related circuits, nine from Dongping and related circuits, seven from Shandong, seven from Hedong, nine from Henan, five from Sichuan, two from Yunnan, two from Gansu, one from Lingbei, five from Shaanxi, two from Liaoyang, and one from Eastern Campaign.

sentences.zh: 南人取合格者七十五人：湖廣一十八人，江浙二十八人，江西二十二人，河南七人。

translations.literal: Southern people who passed selection numbered seventy-five: Huguang eighteen, Jiang-Zhe twenty-eight, Jiangxi twenty-two, Henan seven.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-five southern candidates were to pass: eighteen from Huguang, twenty-eight from Jiang-Zhe, twenty-two from Jiangxi, and seven from Henan.

sentences.zh: 鄉試、會試，許將《禮部韻略》外，余並不許懷挾文字。

translations.literal: For provincial and metropolitan examinations, aside from bringing the Ministry of Rites Rhyme Compendium, all other carrying of written texts is forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In provincial and metropolitan examinations, candidates may bring only the Ministry of Rites Rhyme Compendium; no other written materials may be carried in.

sentences.zh: 差搜檢懷挾官一員，每舉人一名差軍一名看守，無軍人處，差巡軍。

translations.literal: One official is appointed to search for concealed texts; for each candidate one soldier is assigned to guard; where there are no soldiers, patrol soldiers are assigned.
translations.idiomatic: One official is appointed to search for concealed materials; each candidate is assigned one soldier as guard, or a patrol soldier where no regular troops are available.

sentences.zh: 提點擗掠試院，差廉幹官一員，度地安置席舍，務令隔遠，仍自試官入院後，常川妨職，監押外門。

translations.literal: To supervise and secure the examination grounds, one upright and capable official is appointed to measure the ground and place seats and shelters, striving to keep them far apart; from the time examination officials enter the grounds, he shall constantly remain on duty obstructing his other office and guard the outer gate.
translations.idiomatic: An upright official is appointed to secure the examination grounds, lay out seats at adequate distance, and from the time examiners enter the compound remain on duty at the outer gate.

sentences.zh: 鄉試、會試，彌封、謄錄、對讀官下吏人，於各衙門從便差設。

translations.literal: For provincial and metropolitan examinations, the subordinate clerks under sealing, copying, and collation officials are assigned as convenient from each yamen.
translations.idiomatic: For provincial and metropolitan examinations, clerks under the sealing, copying, and collation officials are assigned from the various offices as convenient.

sentences.zh: 試卷不考格，犯御名廟諱及文理紕繆、塗註乙五十字以上者，不考。

translations.literal: Examination papers not meeting standards—those violating imperial names and temple taboos, or with confused reasoning and more than fifty characters of correction and insertion—are not examined.
translations.idiomatic: Papers failing to meet standards—those violating imperial or temple taboos, showing confused reasoning, or containing more than fifty corrections—are not graded.

sentences.zh: 謄錄所承受試卷，並用朱書謄錄正文，實計塗註乙字數，標寫對讀無差，將朱卷逐旋送考試所。

translations.literal: The copying office receives examination papers, all copied in red ink for the main text, actually counting characters of correction and insertion, marking collation without discrepancy, and sending the red copies in succession to the examination office.
translations.idiomatic: The copying office receives the papers, transcribes the main text in red ink, counts all corrections, marks successful collation, and forwards the red copies to the examination office.

sentences.zh: 如朱卷有塗註乙字，亦皆標寫字數，謄錄官書押。

translations.literal: If the red copy has characters of correction and insertion, the number of characters is also marked and written; the copying official signs and seals.
translations.idiomatic: Any corrections on the red copy are likewise counted and marked, and the copying official signs and seals the document.

sentences.zh: 候考校合格，中選人數已定，抄錄字號，索上元卷，請監試官、知貢舉官、同試官，對號開拆。

translations.literal: When examination and assessment are complete and the number selected is fixed, the character numbers are copied, the original rolls are sought, and the supervising examination official, Director of Tribute Presentation, and associate examination officials are invited to open and unpack by number.
translations.idiomatic: Once grading is complete and the number of successful candidates fixed, the code numbers are recorded, the original papers retrieved, and the supervising examiner, Director of Tribute Presentation, and associate examiners open them by number.

sentences.zh: 舉人試卷，各人自備三場文卷並草卷，各一十二幅，於卷首書三代、籍貫、年甲，前期半月於印卷所投納。

translations.literal: Candidates' examination papers: each person prepares examination rolls for three sessions and draft rolls, twelve sheets each, writing three generations, native place, and age at the head of the roll; half a month beforehand they are submitted at the roll-stamping office.
translations.idiomatic: Each candidate prepares examination and draft papers for all three sessions, twelve sheets per roll, with three generations, native place, and age written at the head; these are submitted to the stamping office half a month in advance.

sentences.zh: 置簿收附，用印鈐縫訖，各還舉人。

translations.literal: A register is kept for receipt, seals are applied along the stitched seam, and each is returned to the candidate.
translations.idiomatic: A register records receipt, seals are applied along the stitched seam, and the papers are returned to each candidate.

sentences.zh: 凡就試之日，日未出入場，黃昏納卷。

translations.literal: On the day of examination, before the sun has risen they enter the grounds; at dusk they submit their rolls.
translations.idiomatic: On examination day candidates enter before sunrise and submit their papers at dusk.

sentences.zh: 受卷官送彌封所，撰字號，封彌訖，送謄錄所。

translations.literal: The roll-receiving official sends them to the sealing office, composes character numbers, completes sealing, and sends them to the copying office.
translations.idiomatic: The roll-receiving official forwards them to the sealing office, assigns code numbers, completes sealing, and sends them to the copying office.

sentences.zh: 科舉既行之後，若有各路歲貢及保舉儒人等文字到官，並令還赴本鄉應試。

translations.literal: After the civil examination has been implemented, if documents arrive at offices regarding annual tribute from the circuits or recommended Confucians, all are ordered to return to their native district to take the examination.
translations.idiomatic: Once the civil examination was in force, candidates holding circuit tribute credentials or recommendation documents were ordered to return to their home districts to sit for the examination.

sentences.zh: 倡優之家及患廢疾、若犯十惡奸盜之人，不許應試。

translations.literal: Households of actors and entertainers, those afflicted with crippling illness, and those who have committed the ten abominations or theft and robbery are not permitted to take the examination.
translations.idiomatic: Members of actors' and entertainers' households, the seriously disabled, and those guilty of the ten abominations or theft and robbery were barred from the examination.

sentences.zh: 舉人於試場內，毋得喧嘩，違者治罪，仍殿二舉。

translations.literal: Candidates within the examination grounds must not clamor or shout; violators are punished and additionally deferred for two examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates must not make noise within the examination grounds; violators are punished and barred from the next two examinations.

sentences.zh: 舉人與考試官有五服內親者，自須回避，仍令同試官考卷。

translations.literal: If a candidate and an examination official are related within the five degrees of mourning, they must themselves withdraw; the associate examination official is still ordered to grade the paper.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates related to an examiner within the five degrees of mourning must declare the relationship and withdraw; the associate examiner grades the paper instead.

sentences.zh: 若應避而不自陳者，殿一舉。

translations.literal: If one ought to withdraw but does not declare it oneself, defer one examination.
translations.idiomatic: Failure to declare a required withdrawal results in deferral for one examination.

sentences.zh: 鄉試、會試，若有懷挾及令人代作者，漢人、南人有居父母喪服應舉者，並殿二舉。

translations.literal: In provincial and metropolitan examinations, if there is carrying concealed materials or having another person write in one's place, or Han and southern people who take the examination while in mourning for parents—all are deferred for two examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In provincial and metropolitan examinations, carrying concealed materials, employing a substitute writer, or sitting for the examination while in mourning for parents (for Han and southern candidates) all incur deferral for two examinations.

sentences.zh: 國子監學歲貢生員及伴讀出身，並依舊制，願試者聽。

translations.literal: Directorate of Education annual tribute students and those who came through companion-reading service all follow the old system; those who wish to take the examination are permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Directorate students on annual tribute and those who entered through companion-reading service followed the old rules; those who wished to sit for the examination were permitted.

sentences.zh: 中選者，於監學合得資品上從優銓註。

translations.literal: Those selected receive preferential assessment and appointment one grade above the qualification grade due from the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Those who passed received appointment one grade above their Directorate qualification.

sentences.zh: 別路附籍蒙古、色目、漢人，大都、上都有恒產、住經年深者，從兩都官司，依上例推舉就試，其餘去處冒貫者治罪。

translations.literal: Mongols, persons of other colors, and Han people registered in another circuit who in Dadu and Shangdu have permanent property and have resided for many years follow the two-capital offices in recommendation for examination according to the above precedent; elsewhere those who falsely claim native registration are punished.
translations.idiomatic: Mongols, persons of other colors, and Han registered in another circuit but with permanent property and long residence in Dadu or Shangdu were recommended for examination by the two-capital offices under the above rules; false registration elsewhere was punished.

sentences.zh: 知貢舉以下官會集至公堂，議擬合行事目云：

translations.literal: The Director of Tribute Presentation and officials below assembled in the Hall of Ultimate Justice and deliberated the matters to be jointly carried out, stating:
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Tribute Presentation and subordinate officials assembled in the Hall of Ultimate Justice and drafted the regulations to be carried out, as follows:

sentences.zh: 諸輒於彌封所取問舉人試卷封號姓名及漏泄者，治罪。

translations.literal: As to those who rashly at the sealing office inquire into candidates' examination roll seal numbers and names, or leak them—punish.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who at the sealing office inquires into a candidate's code number or name, or leaks such information, shall be punished.

sentences.zh: 諸試題未出而漏泄者，許人告首。

translations.literal: As to those who leak examination topics before they are issued—informants are permitted to report.
translations.idiomatic: Leaking examination topics before they are issued may be reported by informants.

sentences.zh: 諸對讀試卷官不躬親而輒令人吏對讀，其對讀訖而差誤有礙考校者，有罰。

translations.literal: As to collation officials who do not personally collate but rashly have clerks collate, and after collation there are errors impeding examination—there is punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Collation officials who delegate collation to clerks rather than performing it personally, when errors impede grading, are subject to punishment.

sentences.zh: 諸謄錄人書寫不慎及錯誤有礙考校者，重事責罰。

translations.literal: As to copyists who write carelessly and whose errors impede examination—serious matters are punished severely.
translations.idiomatic: Copyists whose careless writing or errors impede grading are severely punished.

sentences.zh: 諸官司故縱舉人私將試卷出院，及祗應人知而為傳送者，許人告首。

translations.literal: As to offices that deliberately allow candidates to take examination rolls out of the grounds, and attendants who know and transmit them—informants are permitted to report.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who deliberately allow candidates to remove examination papers, or attendants who knowingly transmit them, may be reported by informants.

sentences.zh: 諸監試官掌試院事，不得干預考校。

translations.literal: Supervising examination officials manage examination-ground affairs and must not interfere in examination and assessment.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising examination officials manage the examination grounds and must not interfere in grading.

sentences.zh: 諸試院官在簾內者，不許與簾外官交語。

translations.literal: Examination-ground officials inside the curtain are not permitted to converse with officials outside the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: Officials inside the examination curtain may not converse with those outside it.

sentences.zh: 諸色人無故不得入試廳。

translations.literal: Persons of all categories without cause must not enter the examination hall.
translations.idiomatic: No unauthorized persons may enter the examination hall.

sentences.zh: 諸舉人謗毀主司，率眾喧競，不服止約者，治罪。

translations.literal: Candidates who slander the chief examiners, lead crowds in clamorous dispute, and do not submit to restraint—punish.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates who slander the chief examiners, incite noisy disturbances, or refuse to obey orders are punished.

sentences.zh: 諸舉人就試，無故不冠及擅移坐次者，或偶與親姻鄰坐而不自陳者，懷挾代筆傳義者，並扶出。

translations.literal: Candidates taking the examination who without cause do not wear caps or rashly move their seat order, or happen to sit next to kin by marriage without declaring it, or carry concealed materials, substitute writing, or transmit meaning—all are assisted out.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates who enter without caps, change seats without permission, sit beside relatives without declaring it, or carry concealed materials, use substitute writers, or pass answers are escorted out.

sentences.zh: 諸拆毀試卷首家狀者，推治。

translations.literal: Those who tear and destroy the family-status sheet at the head of the examination roll—investigate and punish.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who tears off the family-status sheet at the head of an examination paper is investigated and punished.

sentences.zh: 諸舉人於試卷書他語者，駁放；

translations.literal: Candidates who write other language on examination rolls are rejected and dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: Candidates who write extraneous matter on their papers are rejected;

sentences.zh: 涉謗訕者，推治。

translations.literal: those involving slander and ridicule are investigated and punished.
translations.idiomatic: those involving slander are investigated and punished.

sentences.zh: 諸試日，為舉人傳送文書，及因而受財者，並許人告。

translations.literal: On examination days, those who transmit documents for candidates and thereby receive property—all may be reported.
translations.idiomatic: On examination days, anyone who transmits documents for candidates or accepts payment for doing so may be reported.

sentences.zh: 諸舉人於別紙上起草者，出榜退落。

translations.literal: Candidates who draft on separate paper are posted on the list as dismissed and rejected.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates who draft on separate paper are posted as failed.

sentences.zh: 諸科文內不得自敘苦辛門第，委謄錄所點檢得，如有違犯，更不謄錄，移文考試院出榜退落。

translations.literal: Within examination compositions one must not narrate one's own hardships or family status; this is entrusted to the copying office for inspection. If there is violation, no further copying is done, documents are sent to the examination office, and the list is posted as dismissal and rejection.
translations.idiomatic: Compositions must not include personal hardship or family background; the copying office inspects for violations. Offending papers are not copied, the examination office is notified, and the candidate is posted as failed.

sentences.zh: 諸冒名就試，別立姓名，反受財為人懷挾代筆傳義者，並許人告。

translations.literal: Those who test under false names, establish separate names, or conversely receive property to carry concealed materials, substitute writing, or transmit meaning for others—all may be reported.
translations.idiomatic: False registration, use of alternate names, or accepting payment to carry materials, write for others, or pass answers may all be reported.

sentences.zh: 諸被黜而妄訴者，治罪。

translations.literal: Those dismissed who make reckless appeals—punish.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates dismissed who lodge frivolous appeals are punished.

sentences.zh: 諸監門官譏察出入，其物應入者，拆封點檢。

translations.literal: Gate-guard officials inspect entry and exit; items that should enter are unsealed and inspected point by point.
translations.idiomatic: Gate guards inspect all entry and exit; permitted items are unsealed and inspected.

sentences.zh: 諸巡鋪官及兵級，不得喧擾，及輒視試文，並容縱舉人無故往來，非因公事，不得與舉人私語。

translations.literal: Patrol officials and soldiers must not create disturbance, must not rashly view examination compositions, must not allow candidates to come and go without cause; except for public business they must not privately converse with candidates.
translations.idiomatic: Patrol officers and soldiers must not cause disturbance, view examination papers, or allow candidates to move about without cause; they may not speak privately with candidates except on official business.

sentences.zh: 諸試卷彌封用印訖，以三不成字為號標寫，仍於塗註乙處用印。

translations.literal: When examination rolls are sealed and stamped, three incomplete characters are used as the number for marking; seals are still applied at places of correction and insertion.
translations.idiomatic: After sealing and stamping, each paper is marked with a code of three incomplete characters, with seals also applied at correction marks.

sentences.zh: 每舉人一名，給祗應巡軍一人，隔夜入院，分宿席房。

translations.literal: For each candidate one attendant patrol soldier is provided; they enter the grounds overnight and lodge separately in seat rooms.
translations.idiomatic: Each candidate is assigned one attendant patrol soldier, who enters the grounds overnight and lodges in the assigned seat room.

sentences.zh: 試日，擊鐘為節。

translations.literal: On examination day, striking the bell serves as the measure.
translations.idiomatic: On examination day, the bell marks each stage of the proceedings.

sentences.zh: 一次，院官以下皆盥漱。

translations.literal: First stroke: all officials of the grounds and below wash and rinse.
translations.idiomatic: At the first bell, all examination officials wash and prepare.

sentences.zh: 二次，監門官啟鑰，舉人入院，搜檢訖，就將解據呈納。

translations.literal: Second stroke: the gate-guard official opens the lock; candidates enter the grounds; after search and inspection they present their credentials of release.
translations.idiomatic: At the second bell the gate guard unlocks the gates; candidates enter, are searched, and present their credentials.

sentences.zh: 禮生贊曰「舉人再拜」，知貢舉官隔簾受一拜，跪答一拜，試官受一拜，答一拜。

translations.literal: The ceremonial attendant announces "Candidate double bow"; the Director of Tribute Presentation receives one bow through the curtain, kneels and returns one bow; the examination official receives one bow and returns one bow.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial attendant calls "Candidate, bow twice." The Director of Tribute Presentation receives one bow through the curtain and returns it kneeling; the examiner receives and returns one bow.

sentences.zh: 鐘三次，頒題，就次。

translations.literal: Third bell stroke: topics are issued; they take their places.
translations.idiomatic: At the third bell the topics are distributed and candidates take their seats.

sentences.zh: 日午，賜膳。

translations.literal: At midday, food is bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: At midday, food is provided.

sentences.zh: 其納卷首，赴受卷所揖而退，不得交語。

translations.literal: When submitting their rolls, they go to the roll-receiving office, bow and withdraw, and must not converse.
translations.idiomatic: When submitting papers, candidates bow at the roll-receiving office and withdraw without speaking.

sentences.zh: 受卷官書舉人姓名於歷，舉人揖而退，取解據出院，巡軍亦出。

translations.literal: The roll-receiving official writes the candidate's name in the register; the candidate bows and withdraws, takes credentials and leaves the grounds; the patrol soldier also leaves.
translations.idiomatic: The roll-receiving official records the candidate's name; the candidate bows, collects credentials, and leaves with the patrol soldier.

sentences.zh: 至晚，鳴鐘一次，鎖院門。

translations.literal: By evening, the bell sounds once and the examination-ground gate is locked.
translations.idiomatic: In the evening the bell sounds once and the examination grounds are locked.

sentences.zh: 第二場，舉人入院，依前搜檢，每十人一甲，序立至公堂下，作揖畢，頒題就次。

translations.literal: Second session: candidates enter the grounds, searched as before; every ten form one company, stand in order below the Hall of Ultimate Justice, bow when finished, topics are issued and they take their places.
translations.idiomatic: In the second session candidates enter and are searched as before; in groups of ten they stand below the Hall of Ultimate Justice, bow, receive the topics, and take their seats.

sentences.zh: 第三場，如前儀。

translations.literal: Third session: as in the previous ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The third session follows the same ceremony.

sentences.zh: 其受卷官具受到試卷，逐旋關發彌封官，將家狀草卷，腰封用印，蒙古、色目、漢人、南人分卷，以三不成字撰號。

translations.literal: The roll-receiving official prepares the received examination rolls, sends them in succession to the sealing official, takes family-status and draft rolls, seals them at the waist with stamps, separates Mongol, person of other color, Han, and southern rolls, and composes numbers from three incomplete characters.
translations.idiomatic: The roll-receiving official forwards the papers to the sealing office, which seals the family-status and draft rolls at the waist, separates Mongol, other-color, Han, and southern rolls, and assigns codes of three incomplete characters.

sentences.zh: 每名累場同用一號，於卷上親書，及於歷內標附訖，牒送謄錄官置歷，分給吏人，並用朱書謄錄正文，仍具元卷塗註乙及謄錄塗註乙字數，卷末書謄錄人姓名，謄錄官具銜書押，用印鈐縫，牒送對讀所。

translations.literal: Each person uses the same number across accumulated sessions; it is personally written on the roll and marked and attached in the register; documents are sent to the copying official to set up the register, distributed to clerks, all copying the main text in red ink, still providing the original roll's corrections and the copying corrections' character counts; at the roll's end the copyist's name is written; the copying official provides title, signs, and seals, applies stamps along the seam, and sends documents to the collation office.
translations.idiomatic: Each candidate uses one code number across all sessions, written on the roll and recorded in the register. The copying office distributes papers to clerks, who transcribe the main text in red ink, count corrections on both original and copy, sign the end of each roll, seal the seam, and forward papers to the collation office.

sentences.zh: 翰林掾史具謄錄訖試卷總數，呈報監察御史。

translations.literal: The Hanlin clerk prepares the total number of copied examination rolls completed and reports to the investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanlin clerk reports the total number of copied papers to the investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 對讀官以元卷與朱卷躬親對讀無差，具銜書押，呈解貢院，元卷發還彌封所。

translations.literal: The collation official personally collates the original roll with the red copy without discrepancy, provides title and signs, presents and releases to the tribute-presenting grounds; the original roll is sent back to the sealing office.
translations.idiomatic: The collation official personally compares original and red copy, signs, submits the papers to the tribute-presenting grounds, and returns the originals to the sealing office.

sentences.zh: 各所行移，並用朱書，試卷照依元號附簿。

translations.literal: All transmitted documents from each office use red ink; examination rolls are attached to registers according to the original numbers.
translations.idiomatic: All official documents are written in red ink, and examination papers are filed by their original code numbers.

sentences.zh: 試官考卷，知貢舉居中，試官相對向坐，公同考校，分作三等，逐等又分上中下，用墨筆批點。

translations.literal: Examination officials grade the rolls; the Director of Tribute Presentation sits in the center, examination officials sit facing each other, jointly examining and assessing, dividing into three grades, each grade further divided into upper, middle, and lower, marking with ink brush.
translations.idiomatic: Examiners grade the papers with the Director of Tribute Presentation seated in the center and associate examiners facing each other. Papers are divided into three grades, each subdivided into upper, middle, and lower, and marked in ink.

sentences.zh: 考校既定，收掌試卷官於號簿內標寫分數，知貢舉官、同試官、監察御史、彌封官，公同取上元卷對號開拆，知貢舉於試卷家狀上親書省試第幾名。

translations.literal: When examination and assessment are settled, the official in charge of examination rolls marks scores in the number register; the Director of Tribute Presentation, associate examination officials, investigating censor, and sealing official jointly take the original rolls and open by number; the Director of Tribute Presentation personally writes on the family-status sheet of the examination roll the metropolitan examination rank number.
translations.idiomatic: Once grading is complete, the paper custodian records scores in the register. The Director of Tribute Presentation, associate examiners, investigating censor, and sealing official jointly open the original papers by number, and the director writes each candidate's metropolitan rank on the family-status sheet.

sentences.zh: 拆號既畢，應有試卷並付禮部架閣，貢舉諸官出院。

translations.literal: When opening by number is finished, all examination rolls are delivered to the Ministry of Rites archive, and the tribute-presenting officials leave the grounds.
translations.idiomatic: When all numbers have been opened, the papers are deposited in the Ministry of Rites archive and the examination officials leave the grounds.

sentences.zh: 中書省以中選舉人分為二榜，揭於省門之左右。

translations.literal: The Secretariat divides selected candidates into two rosters and posts them to the left and right of the Secretariat gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat posts the successful candidates in two rosters to the left and right of the Secretariat gate.

sentences.zh: 三月初四日，中書省奏準，以初七日禦試舉人於翰林國史院，定委監試官及諸執事。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the third month, the Secretariat memorialized approval to conduct the palace examination of candidates on the seventh day at the Hanlin National History Academy, fixing appointment of supervising examination officials and all attendants.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the third month the Secretariat reported approval to hold the palace examination at the Hanlin National History Academy on the seventh, appointing supervising examiners and all attendants.

sentences.zh: 初五日，各官入院。

translations.literal: On the fifth day, all officials enter the grounds.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day all officials entered the examination grounds.

sentences.zh: 初六日，撰策問進呈，俟上采取。

translations.literal: On the sixth day, policy questions are drafted and presented, awaiting the ruler's selection.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth day policy questions were drafted and presented for the emperor's selection.

sentences.zh: 初七日，執事者望闕設案於堂前，置策題於上。

translations.literal: On the seventh day, attendants facing the palace set a table before the hall and placed the policy topic upon it.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day attendants set a table before the hall facing the palace and placed the policy topic upon it.

sentences.zh: 舉人入院，搜檢訖，蒙古人作一甲，序立，禮生導引至於堂前，望闕兩拜，賜策題，又兩拜，各就次。

translations.literal: Candidates enter the grounds; after search and inspection, Mongols form one company, stand in order, ceremonial attendants guide them before the hall, they bow twice toward the palace, receive the policy topic, bow twice again, and each takes his place.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates entered and were searched. Mongols formed one company, were led before the hall, bowed twice toward the palace, received the policy topic, bowed again, and took their seats.

sentences.zh: 色目人作一甲，漢人、南人作一甲，如前儀。

translations.literal: Persons of other colors form one company; Han people and southern people form one company, as in the previous ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Persons of other colors formed one company; Han and southern candidates formed another, following the same ceremony.

sentences.zh: 每進士一人，差蒙古宿衛士一人監視。

translations.literal: For each presented scholar one Mongol palace guard is assigned to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: Each presented scholar was assigned one Mongol palace guard to supervise.

sentences.zh: 日午，賜膳。

translations.literal: At midday, food is bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: At midday, food was provided.

sentences.zh: 進士納卷畢，出院。

translations.literal: When presented scholars have submitted their rolls, they leave the grounds.
translations.idiomatic: When the presented scholars had submitted their papers, they left the grounds.

sentences.zh: 監試官同讀卷官，以所對策第其高下，分為三甲進奏。

translations.literal: The supervising examination official together with the reading official ranks the policy responses by high and low, divides them into three classes, and presents a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising examiner and reading official ranked the policy responses and divided them into three classes for presentation to the throne.

sentences.zh: 作二榜，用敕黃紙書，揭於內前紅門之左右。

translations.literal: Two rosters are made, written on imperial yellow paper, and posted to the left and right of the inner front red gate.
translations.idiomatic: Two rosters were written on imperial yellow paper and posted to the left and right of the inner red gate.

sentences.zh: 前一日，禮部告諭中選進士，以次日詣闕前，所司具香案，侍儀舍人唱名，謝恩，放榜。

translations.literal: The day before, the Ministry of Rites announces to selected presented scholars that on the next day they shall proceed before the palace; the responsible office prepares the incense table, ceremonial attendants call names, they give thanks for grace, and the roster is released.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, the Ministry of Rites notified the successful presented scholars to appear before the palace the next day. The responsible office prepared the incense table, ceremonial attendants called names, the scholars gave thanks, and the roster was published.

sentences.zh: 擇日賜恩榮宴於翰林國史院，押宴以中書省官，凡預試官並與宴。

translations.literal: On a chosen day the grace-and-glory banquet is bestowed at the Hanlin National History Academy; a Secretariat official presides over the banquet, and all who participated in the examination also join the banquet.
translations.idiomatic: On a chosen day a banquet of grace and honor was held at the Hanlin National History Academy, presided over by a Secretariat official; all examination officials attended.

sentences.zh: 預宴官及進士並簪華至所居。

translations.literal: Banquet officials and presented scholars all wear flowers in their hair to their residences.
translations.idiomatic: Banquet officials and presented scholars wore flowers in their hair as they proceeded to their lodgings.

sentences.zh: 擇日恭詣殿廷，上謝恩表。
