translations.literal: On a chosen day they respectfully proceed to the palace hall and submit a memorial of thanks for grace.
translations.idiomatic: On a chosen day they respectfully proceeded to the palace and submitted a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 次日，詣中書省參見。

translations.literal: The next day, they proceed to the Secretariat for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they paid their respects at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 又擇日，諸進士詣先聖廟行舍菜禮，第一人具祝文行事，刻石題名於國子監。

translations.literal: On another chosen day, all presented scholars proceed to the temple of the former sage to perform the vegetable-offering ceremony; the first place prepares the prayer text and conducts the rite; names are carved in stone at the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: On another chosen day all presented scholars went to the Confucian temple to perform the vegetable-offering ceremony. The top graduate composed and read the prayer; names were carved on stone at the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 泰定元年春三月，廷試進士捌剌、張益等八十有六人。

translations.literal: First year of Taiding, spring, third month: palace examination of presented scholars Balie, Zhang Yi, and others, eighty-six in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of spring in the first year of Taiding, eighty-six presented scholars including Balie and Zhang Yi took the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 四年春三月，廷試進士阿察赤、李黼等八十有六人。

translations.literal: Fourth year, spring, third month: palace examination of presented scholars Achachi, Li Fu, and others, eighty-six in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of spring in the fourth year, eighty-six presented scholars including Achachi and Li Fu took the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 天歷三年春三月，廷試進士篤列圖、王文燁等九十有七人。

translations.literal: Third year of Tianli, spring, third month: palace examination of presented scholars Dulietu, Wang Wenye, and others, ninety-seven in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of spring in the third year of Tianli, ninety-seven presented scholars including Dulietu and Wang Wenye took the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 元統癸酉科，廷試進士同同、李齊等，復增名額，以及百人之數。

translations.literal: Yuantong guiyou cohort: palace examination of presented scholars Tongtong, Li Qi, and others; the quota of names was again increased to reach one hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuantong guiyou examination, presented scholars including Tongtong and Li Qi took the palace examination; the quota was increased to one hundred.

sentences.zh: 稍異其制，左右榜各三人，皆賜進士及第，其餘出身有差。

translations.literal: The system was slightly altered: three persons on each of the left and right rosters were all granted Presented Scholar with Honors; the rest received differentiated origins.
translations.idiomatic: The system was slightly altered: three candidates on each roster received Presented Scholar with Honors; the rest received differentiated ranks.

sentences.zh: 科舉取士，莫盛於斯。

translations.literal: Civil examination recruitment of scholars was never more flourishing than this.
translations.idiomatic: The civil examination never flourished more than at this time.

sentences.zh: 後三年，其制遂罷。

translations.literal: Three years later, the system was then abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later the system was abolished.

sentences.zh: 又七年而復興，遂稍變程式，減蒙古、色目人明經二絳，增本經義；

translations.literal: Seven years later it was revived, and the procedures were then slightly changed: reducing for Mongols and persons of other colors the two threads of Understanding the Classics, and adding classic meaning on one's own classic;
translations.idiomatic: Seven years later it was revived with revised procedures: for Mongols and persons of other colors the two Understanding the Classics questions were reduced and classic exegesis on one's chosen classic was added;

sentences.zh: 易漢、南人第一場《四書》疑一道為本經疑，增第二場古賦外，於詔誥、章表內又科一道。

translations.literal: for Han and southern people the first session's one Four Books doubt question was changed to a doubt question on one's own classic; beyond ancient rhapsody in the second session, within edict-patent and memorial-table one more category was added.
translations.idiomatic: for Han and southern candidates the first-session Four Books question was changed to a question on one's chosen classic; and beyond ancient rhapsody in the second session, one additional question in edict, patent, memorial, or table was added.

sentences.zh: 此有元科目取士之制，大略如此。

translations.literal: This is the Yuan system of examination categories for taking scholars—in rough outline such is the case.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the Yuan examination system for recruiting officials, in broad outline.

sentences.zh: 若夫會試下第者，自延祐創設之初，丞相帖木叠兒、阿散及平章李孟等奏：「下第舉人，年七十以上者，與從七品流官致仕；

translations.literal: As for those who failed the metropolitan examination, from the beginning of the Yanyou founding, Chancellor Temuder, Asan, and Vice Director Li Meng and others memorialized: "Candidates who failed the examination, those seventy years and above shall receive ranked office retirement at rank 7b;
translations.idiomatic: As for those who failed the metropolitan examination, at the founding of the Yanyou system Chancellor Temuder, Asan, and Vice Director Li Meng memorialized: "Failed candidates aged seventy or above shall receive retirement as ranked officials at rank 7b;

sentences.zh: 六十以上者，與教授；

translations.literal: those sixty and above shall receive instructor posts;
translations.idiomatic: those sixty or above shall receive instructor posts;

sentences.zh: 元有出身者，於應得資品上稍優加之；

translations.literal: those who originally had origins shall receive slight preferential addition upon the qualification grade due them;
translations.idiomatic: those who already held official standing shall receive a slight preferential advance above their due qualification grade;

sentences.zh: 無出身者，與山長、學正。

translations.literal: Those without origins receive academy director and school rectifier posts.
translations.idiomatic: those without prior official standing received posts as academy director or school rectifier.

sentences.zh: 受省劄，後舉不為例。

translations.literal: They received provincial documents; later examinations were not taken as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: They received provincial appointment documents, but this was not made a standing precedent.

sentences.zh: 今有來遲而不及應試者，未曾區用。

translations.literal: Now there are those who came late and could not take the examination; they have not yet been assigned use.
translations.idiomatic: Those who arrived too late to sit for the examination had not yet been assigned posts.

sentences.zh: 取旨。」

translations.literal: Seek the imperial decision."
translations.idiomatic: The court sought the emperor's decision."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「依下第例恩之，勿著為格。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Grant favor according to the failed-examination precedent; do not fix it as a regulation."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Grant them favor under the failed-candidate precedent, but do not fix this as a permanent rule."

sentences.zh: 泰定元年三月，中書省臣奏：「下第舉人，仁宗延祐間，命中書省各授教官之職，以慰其歸。

translations.literal: First year of Taiding, third month, Secretariat ministers memorialized: "Failed candidates—in Emperor Renzong's Yanyou era, the Secretariat was ordered to grant each teaching-official posts to comfort them on their return.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the first year of Taiding, Secretariat ministers memorialized: "Under Emperor Renzong's Yanyou reign, failed candidates were given teaching posts by the Secretariat to comfort them on their return home.

sentences.zh: 今當改元之初，恩澤宜溥。

translations.literal: Now at the beginning of a change of reign title, grace and favor should be broad.
translations.idiomatic: Now, at the beginning of a new reign era, favors should be broadly distributed.

sentences.zh: 蒙古、色目人，年三十以上並兩舉不第者，與教授；

translations.literal: Mongols and persons of other colors, thirty years and above who failed two examinations, receive instructor posts;
translations.idiomatic: Mongols and persons of other colors aged thirty or above who failed two examinations shall receive instructor posts;

sentences.zh: 以下，與學正、山長。

translations.literal: below that, receive school rectifier and academy director posts.
translations.idiomatic: those below that age shall receive school rectifier or academy director posts.

sentences.zh: 漢人、南人，年五十以上並兩舉不第者，與教授；

translations.literal: Han people and southern people, fifty years and above who failed two examinations, receive instructor posts;
translations.idiomatic: Han and southern candidates aged fifty or above who failed two examinations shall receive instructor posts;

sentences.zh: 以下，與學正、山長。

translations.literal: below that, receive school rectifier and academy director posts.
translations.idiomatic: those below that age shall receive school rectifier or academy director posts.

sentences.zh: 先有資品出身者，更優加之；

translations.literal: those who already had qualification-grade origins receive further preferential addition;
translations.idiomatic: Those who already held official standing shall receive a further preferential advance;

sentences.zh: 不願仕者，令備國子員。

translations.literal: those unwilling to serve are ordered to prepare as Directorate students.
translations.idiomatic: those unwilling to serve shall be retained as Directorate students.

sentences.zh: 後勿為格。」

translations.literal: Afterward do not make this a regulation."
translations.idiomatic: This shall not become a standing rule thereafter."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The memorial was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 自余下第之士，恩例不可常得，間有試補書吏以登仕籍者。

translations.literal: As for the rest of failed scholars, the grace precedent could not be regularly obtained; occasionally some tested and supplemented as document clerks to enter the service register.
translations.idiomatic: Other failed candidates could not regularly receive such favors; occasionally some passed clerk examinations and entered the official register.

sentences.zh: 惟已廢復興之後，其法始變，下第者悉授以路府學正及書院山長。

translations.literal: Only after the abolished system was revived did the law begin to change: all who failed were granted circuit and prefectural school rectifier and academy director posts.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the examination was revived and then abolished again did the practice change: failed candidates were routinely given posts as circuit or prefectural school rectifier or academy director.

sentences.zh: 又增取鄉試備榜，亦授以郡學錄及縣教諭。

translations.literal: The provincial examination reserve roster was also increased, and those too were granted commandery school recorder and district instructor posts.
translations.idiomatic: The reserve roster for the provincial examination was expanded as well, with appointments as commandery school recorder or district instructor.

sentences.zh: 於是科舉取士，得人為盛焉。

translations.literal: Thus civil examination recruitment of scholars obtained men in great abundance.
translations.idiomatic: At this point the civil examination produced talent in exceptional abundance.

sentences.zh: ○學校

translations.literal: ○ Schools
translations.idiomatic: Schools

sentences.zh: 世祖至元八年春正月，始下詔立京師蒙古國子學，教習諸生，於隨朝蒙古、漢人百官及怯薛歹官員，選子弟俊秀者入學，然未有員數。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu, eighth year of Zhiyuan, spring, first month, first issued an edict establishing the Capital Mongol Directorate of Education to teach the students; from Mongol and Han officials attending court and keshik officers, select sons and younger brothers of outstanding talent to enter study, but there was as yet no quota.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the eighth year of Emperor Shizu's Zhiyuan reign, an edict established the Capital Mongol Directorate of Education. Sons of Mongol and Han officials at court and of keshik officers were selected for study, though no fixed quota was yet set.

sentences.zh: 以《通鑒節要》用蒙古語言譯寫教之，俟生員習學成效，出題試問，觀其所對精通者，量授官職。

translations.literal: The Essentials of the Comprehensive Mirror were translated into Mongol language for teaching; when students' study showed results, topics were issued for trial questioning, and those whose answers showed mastery were measured out official posts.
translations.idiomatic: The Essentials of the Comprehensive Mirror was taught in Mongol translation. When students showed progress they were tested, and those who answered with mastery received official appointments.

sentences.zh: 成宗大德十年春二月，增生員廩膳，通前三十員為六十員。

translations.literal: Emperor Chengzong, tenth year of Dade, spring, second month, increased students' grain stipends, making sixty in all together with the previous thirty.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring in the tenth year of Dade under Emperor Chengzong, student grain stipends were increased from thirty to sixty.

sentences.zh: 武宗至大二年，定伴讀員四十人，以在籍上名生員學問優長者補之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong, second year of Zhide, fixed companion-reading posts at forty persons, filled from registered named students of superior learning.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhide under Emperor Wuzong, forty companion-reader posts were established, filled from registered students of superior accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 仁宗延祐二年冬十月，以所設生員百人，蒙古五十人，色目二十人，漢人三十人，而百官子弟之就學者，常不下二三百人，宜增其廩餼，乃減去庶民子弟一百一十四員，聽陪堂學業，於見供生員一百名外，量增五十名。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong, second year of Yanyou, tenth month of winter: because the established students numbered one hundred—fifty Mongols, twenty persons of other colors, thirty Han—and sons of the myriad officials entering study commonly were not fewer than two or three hundred, their grain stipends ought to be increased; thereupon one hundred fourteen commoner sons were removed, permitted to follow hall study, and beyond the presently supplied one hundred students fifty more were added by measure.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter of the second year of Yanyou under Emperor Renzong, the school had set quotas of one hundred students—fifty Mongols, twenty persons of other colors, and thirty Han—but children of officials in attendance often exceeded two or three hundred. Their stipends were therefore increased by removing one hundred fourteen commoners from the regular rolls, allowing them to study in the hall without full stipend, and adding fifty places beyond the existing one hundred funded students.

sentences.zh: 元置蒙古二十人，漢人三十人，其生員紙劄筆墨止給三十人，歲凡二次給之。

translations.literal: Originally established were twenty Mongols and thirty Han; students' paper, documents, brush, and ink were supplied only to thirty persons, given twice a year in all.
translations.idiomatic: The original quotas were twenty Mongols and thirty Han. Paper, documents, brush, and ink were supplied only to thirty students, disbursed twice yearly.

sentences.zh: 至元六年秋七月，置諸路蒙古字學。

translations.literal: Sixth year of Zhiyuan, autumn, seventh month: Mongol Script Schools were established in all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn in the sixth year of Zhiyuan, Mongol Script Schools were established throughout the circuits.

sentences.zh: 十二月，中書省定學制頒行之，命諸路府官子弟入學，上路二人，下路二人，府一人，州一人。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, the Secretariat fixed the school system and promulgated it, ordering sons of circuit and prefectural officials to enter study: two per superior circuit, two per inferior circuit, one per prefecture, one per subprefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Secretariat finalized and promulgated the school regulations, requiring sons of circuit and prefectural officials to enroll: two each for superior and inferior circuits, one each for prefecture and subprefecture.

sentences.zh: 余民間子弟，上路三十人，下路二十五人。

translations.literal: The remaining commoner sons: thirty per superior circuit, twenty-five per inferior circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Commoner students were capped at thirty per superior circuit and twenty-five per inferior circuit.

sentences.zh: 願充生徒者，與免一身雜役。

translations.literal: Those willing to serve as students were granted exemption from miscellaneous corvée for one person.
translations.idiomatic: Volunteer students were exempted from personal miscellaneous corvée duties.

sentences.zh: 以譯寫《通鑒節要》頒行各路，俾肄習之。

translations.literal: The translated Essentials of the Comprehensive Mirror was issued to all circuits for their diligent study.
translations.idiomatic: A Mongol translation of the Essentials of the Comprehensive Mirror was distributed to every circuit for study.

sentences.zh: 至成宗大德五年冬十月，又定生員，散府二十人，上、中州十五人，下州十人。

translations.literal: By Emperor Chengzong, fifth year of Dade, tenth month of winter, student quotas were again fixed: twenty per scattered prefecture, fifteen per superior and middle subprefecture, ten per inferior subprefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter of the fifth year of Dade under Emperor Chengzong, quotas were reset at twenty for scattered prefectures, fifteen for superior and middle subprefectures, and ten for inferior subprefectures.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年，命有司割地，給諸路蒙古學生員餼廩。

translations.literal: First year of Yuanzhen, officials were ordered to assign land and supply grain stipends to Mongol students in all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanzhen, authorities were ordered to allocate land to fund grain stipends for Mongol students in each circuit.

sentences.zh: 其學官，至元十九年，定擬路府州設教授，以國字在諸字之右，府州教授一任，準從八品，再歷路教授一任，準正八品，任回本等遷轉。

translations.literal: Their school officers: in the nineteenth year of Zhiyuan, it was decided that circuits, prefectures, and subprefectures should establish instructors; the national script ranked above all scripts; one term as prefectural instructor corresponded to Associate Eighth Rank, one further term as circuit instructor corresponded to Regular Eighth Rank, and upon completion one reverted to advancement within one's original grade.
translations.idiomatic: School appointments were regulated in the nineteenth year of Zhiyuan. Circuits, prefectures, and subprefectures each received instructors, with the national script taking precedence over all others. A single term as prefectural instructor ranked at Associate Eighth Grade; after a further term as circuit instructor, at Regular Eighth Grade, after which one returned to promotion within one's original grade.

sentences.zh: 大德四年，添設學正一員，上自國學，下及州縣，舉生員高等，從翰林考試，凡學官譯史，取以充焉。

translations.literal: Fourth year of Dade, one school rectifier was added; from the National University down to districts and counties, superior students were selected and examined by the Hanlin Academy; all school officers and translators were drawn from them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Dade an additional school rectifier post was created. From the National University down to district and county schools, top students were examined by the Hanlin Academy and appointed as school officers or translators.

sentences.zh: 太宗六年癸巳，以馮誌常為國子學總教，命侍臣子弟十八人入學。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong, sixth year, guisi year, appointed Feng Zhichang as chief instructor of the Directorate of the Sons of the State, and ordered eighteen sons of attendant ministers to enter study.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taizong (the guisi year), Feng Zhichang was made chief instructor of the Directorate of the Sons of the State, and eighteen sons of court ministers were enrolled.

sentences.zh: 世祖至元七年，命侍臣子弟十有一人入學，以長者四人從許衡，童子七人從王恂。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu, seventh year of Zhiyuan, ordered eleven sons of attendant ministers to enter study: four elders followed Xu Heng, seven youths followed Wang Xun.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan under Emperor Shizu, eleven sons of court ministers entered the school: four older students under Xu Heng and seven younger ones under Wang Xun.

sentences.zh: 至二十四年，立國子學，而定其制。

translations.literal: By the twenty-fourth year, the Directorate of the Sons of the State was established and its system fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year the Directorate of the Sons of the State was formally established and its regulations set.

sentences.zh: 設博士，通掌學事，分教三齋生員，講授經旨，是正音訓，上嚴教導之術，下考肄習之業。

translations.literal: Erudites were established to oversee all school affairs in general, divide instruction among students of the three halls, lecture on classic meaning, correct pronunciation and glosses, above enforcing methods of instruction, below examining the work of diligent study.
translations.idiomatic: Erudites were appointed to direct all academic affairs, teaching the three halls, expounding the classics, and correcting pronunciation. They oversaw instruction above and examined students' progress below.

sentences.zh: 復設助教，同掌學事，而專守一齋；

translations.literal: Assistant erudites were further established to share oversight of school affairs while each guarding one hall exclusively;
translations.idiomatic: Assistant erudites were also appointed to share academic oversight, each responsible for one hall;

sentences.zh: 正、錄，申明規矩，督習課業。

translations.literal: rectifiers and recorders clarified regulations and supervised study of lessons.
translations.idiomatic: rectifiers and recorders enforced the rules and supervised coursework.

sentences.zh: 凡讀書必先《孝經》、《小學》、《論語》、《孟子》、《大學》、《中庸》，次及《詩》、《書》、《禮記》、《周禮》、《春秋》、《易》。

translations.literal: For all reading, one must first the Classic of Filial Piety, Elementary Learning, Analects, Mencius, Great Learning, and Doctrine of the Mean, then proceed to the Odes, Documents, Record of Rites, Rites of Zhou, Spring and Autumn Annals, and Changes.
translations.idiomatic: The curriculum began with the Classic of Filial Piety, Elementary Learning, Analects, Mencius, Great Learning, and Doctrine of the Mean, then advanced to the Odes, Documents, Record of Rites, Rites of Zhou, Spring and Autumn Annals, and Changes.

sentences.zh: 博士、助教親授句讀、音訓，正、錄、伴讀以次傳習之。

translations.literal: Erudites and assistant erudites personally taught punctuation, reading, and glosses; rectifiers, recorders, and companion-readers transmitted study in order.
translations.idiomatic: Erudites and assistants taught punctuation and glosses directly; rectifiers, recorders, and companion-readers passed the lessons down in sequence.

sentences.zh: 講說則依所讀之序，正、錄、伴讀亦以次而傳習之。

translations.literal: For lectures, the order of what was read was followed; rectifiers, recorders, and companion-readers likewise transmitted study in order.
translations.idiomatic: Lectures followed the reading sequence, and rectifiers, recorders, and companion-readers continued instruction in the same order.

sentences.zh: 次日，抽簽，令諸生復說其功課。

translations.literal: The next day, lots were drawn, ordering the students to recite again their lessons.
translations.idiomatic: The next day lots were drawn and students were made to recite their lessons from memory.

sentences.zh: 對屬、詩章、經解、史評，則博士出題，生員具稿，先呈助教，俟博士既定，始錄附課簿，以憑考校。

translations.literal: For paired composition, poetry, classic exegesis, and historical critique, the erudite set topics; students prepared drafts, first presented them to the assistant erudite, and only after the erudite had determined them were they recorded in the lesson book for reference in examination.
translations.idiomatic: For paired composition, verse, classical commentary, and historical critique, erudites set the topics. Students drafted answers, submitted them first to assistants, and only after erudites approved were entries made in the coursework register for grading.

sentences.zh: 其生員之數，定二百人，先令一百人及伴讀二十人入學。

translations.literal: The number of students was fixed at two hundred; first one hundred students and twenty companion-readers were ordered to enter study.
translations.idiomatic: The student quota was set at two hundred, with an initial enrollment of one hundred students and twenty companion-readers.

sentences.zh: 其百人之內，蒙古半之，色目、漢人半之。

translations.literal: Within the one hundred, half were Mongol; persons of other colors and Han formed the other half.
translations.idiomatic: Of the first hundred, half were Mongol and half were persons of other colors and Han combined.

sentences.zh: 許衡又著諸生入學雜儀，及日用節目。

translations.literal: Xu Heng further composed miscellaneous rites for students entering study and daily protocols.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Heng also drafted entrance rites and daily routines for students.

sentences.zh: 七年，命生員八十人入學，俾永為定式而遵行之。

translations.literal: Seventh year, eighty students were ordered to enter study, to be forever the fixed form and followed in practice.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year eighty students were enrolled, and this became the permanent standard.

sentences.zh: 成宗大德八年冬十二月，始定國子生，蒙古、色目、漢人三歲各貢一人。

translations.literal: Emperor Chengzong, eighth year of Dade, twelfth month of winter, first fixed Directorate students: Mongols, persons of other colors, and Han each presented one person every three years.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of winter of the eighth year of Dade under Emperor Chengzong, quotas for Directorate students were first set: one Mongol, one person of other colors, and one Han graduate every three years.

sentences.zh: 十年冬閏十月，國子學定蒙古、色目、漢人生員二百人，三年各貢二人。

translations.literal: Tenth year, intercalary tenth month of winter, the Directorate fixed two hundred Mongol, persons of other colors, and Han students, each category presenting two persons every three years.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary tenth month of winter of the tenth year the Directorate set two hundred students, with two graduates presented from each category every three years.

sentences.zh: 武宗至大四年秋閏七月，定生員額二百人。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong, fourth year of Zhide, intercalary seventh month of autumn, fixed the student quota at two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary seventh month of autumn of the fourth year of Zhide under Emperor Wuzong, the student quota was fixed at two hundred.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月，復立國子學試貢法，蒙古授官六品，色目正七品，漢人從七品。

translations.literal: Twelfth month of winter, the Directorate trial presentation law was re-established: Mongols received Sixth Rank office, persons of other colors Regular Seventh Rank, Han Associate Seventh Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of winter the Directorate examination and presentation system was restored: Mongols received sixth-rank posts, persons of other colors seventh rank, and Han associate seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 試蒙古生之法宜從寬，色目生宜稍加密，漢人生則全科場之制。

translations.literal: The method for testing Mongol students ought to be lenient; for persons of other colors slightly stricter; for Han students the full examination-ground system.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol students were tested leniently, persons of other colors under somewhat stricter standards, and Han students under the full civil examination format.

sentences.zh: 仁宗延祐二年秋八月，增置生員百人，陪堂生二十人，用集賢學士趙孟頫、禮部尚書元明善等所議國子學貢試之法更定之。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong, second year of Yanyou, eighth month of autumn, added one hundred students and twenty hall-companion students, revising according to the Directorate presentation-examination law discussed by Hanlin Academician Zhao Mengfu, Minister of Rites Yuan Mingshan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn of the second year of Yanyou under Emperor Renzong, one hundred students and twenty hall companions were added, and the Directorate presentation examinations were revised along lines proposed by Zhao Mengfu, Yuan Mingshan, and others.

sentences.zh: 一曰升齋等第。

translations.literal: First: Hall advancement grades and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: First: advancement through the halls by grade.

sentences.zh: 六齋東西相向，下兩齋左曰遊藝，右曰依仁，凡誦書講說、小學屬對者隸焉。

translations.literal: Six halls faced east and west; the lower pair: left called Recreation in the Arts, right called Resting in Benevolence—all who recited books, lectured, and did Elementary Learning paired composition belonged there.
translations.idiomatic: Six halls faced each other east and west. The lower pair were Recreation in the Arts (left) and Resting in Benevolence (right), for recitation, elementary lectures, and paired composition from Elementary Learning.

sentences.zh: 中兩齋左曰據德，右曰志道，講說《四書》、課肄詩律者隸焉。

translations.literal: The middle pair: left called Resting in Virtue, right called Aspiring to the Way—for lecturing on the Four Books and drilling poetic rules.
translations.idiomatic: The middle halls were Resting in Virtue (left) and Aspiring to the Way (right), for the Four Books and poetry.

sentences.zh: 上兩齋左曰時習，右曰日新，講說《易》、《書》、《詩》、《春秋》科，習明經義等程文者隸焉。

translations.literal: The upper pair: left called Timely Practice, right called Daily Renewal—for lecturing on the Changes, Documents, Odes, and Spring and Autumn subjects and practicing examination essays on classic meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The upper halls were Timely Practice (left) and Daily Renewal (right), for the Changes, Documents, Odes, Spring and Autumn, and examination essays on classical meaning.

sentences.zh: 每齋員數不等，每季考其所習經書課業，及不違規矩者，以次遞升。

translations.literal: Each hall had unequal numbers of members; each season their studied classics and lessons were examined, and those who did not violate regulations were promoted in order.
translations.idiomatic: Each hall had a different capacity. Quarterly examinations of coursework and conduct determined orderly promotion.

sentences.zh: 二曰私試規矩。

translations.literal: Second: Rules for private examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Second: rules for internal examinations.

sentences.zh: 漢人驗日新、時習兩齋，蒙古色目取志道、據德兩齋，本學舉實歷坐齋二周歲以上，未嘗犯過者，許令充試。

translations.literal: Han were verified in the Daily Renewal and Timely Practice halls; Mongols and persons of other colors in the Aspiring to the Way and Resting in Virtue halls. The school reported those with actual residence in a hall of two full years or more who had never committed an offense; they were permitted to take the trial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Han students qualified from the Daily Renewal and Timely Practice halls; Mongols and persons of other colors from Aspiring to the Way and Resting in Virtue. Students with at least two full years in a hall and no infractions were allowed to sit the internal examination.

sentences.zh: 限實歷坐齋三周歲以上，以充貢舉。

translations.literal: They were limited to actual residence in a hall of three full years or more to qualify for presentation and examination.
translations.idiomatic: Presentation to the civil examinations required at least three full years' residence in a hall.

sentences.zh: 漢人私試，孟月試經疑一道，仲月試經義一道，季月試策問、表章、詔誥科一道。

translations.literal: Han private examinations: first month of the season, one classic doubt; second month, one classic meaning; third month, one policy question, memorial, or edict-proclamation subject.
translations.idiomatic: Han internal exams assigned one classic doubt in the first month of each season, one classic meaning in the second, and one policy question, memorial, or edict in the third.

sentences.zh: 蒙古、色目人，孟、仲月各試明經一道，季月試策問一道。

translations.literal: Mongols and persons of other colors: first and second months each one illuminating-the-classics subject; third month one policy question.
translations.idiomatic: Mongols and persons of other colors took one classics subject in the first two months of each season and one policy question in the third.

sentences.zh: 辭理俱優者為上等，準一分；

translations.literal: Those excellent in both expression and principle ranked superior, credited one point;
translations.idiomatic: Superior answers in both reasoning and style earned one point;

sentences.zh: 理優辭平者為中等，準半分。

translations.literal: principle superior and expression level ranked middle, credited half a point.
translations.idiomatic: sound reasoning with ordinary expression earned half a point.

sentences.zh: 每歲終，通計其年積分，至八分以上者升充高等生員，以四十名為額，內蒙古、色目各十名，漢人二十名。

translations.literal: At each year's end the year's accumulated points were totaled; those reaching eight-tenths of a point or more were promoted to superior students, with a quota of forty names—within them ten Mongols, ten persons of other colors, twenty Han.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end points were totaled. Students scoring at least eight-tenths were promoted to advanced standing, capped at forty—ten Mongols, ten persons of other colors, and twenty Han.

sentences.zh: 歲終試貢，員不必備，惟取實才。

translations.literal: Year-end trial presentation: the quota need not be filled; only real talent was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Year-end presentations did not require a full quota—only genuine ability mattered.

sentences.zh: 有分同闕少者，以坐齋月日先後多少為定。

translations.literal: When points were equal and places few, priority was determined by earlier or later months and days of residence in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Ties for limited slots were broken by length of residence in the hall.

sentences.zh: 其未及等，並雖及等無闕未補者，其年積分，並不為用，下年再行積算。

translations.literal: Those not yet reaching the grade, and those who reached the grade but had no vacancy and were not yet supplemented—their year's accumulated points were all unused; the next year accumulation was calculated anew.
translations.idiomatic: Students who missed the threshold, or met it when no vacancy existed, forfeited that year's points and began accumulating anew.

sentences.zh: 每月初二日蚤旦，圓揖後，本學博士、助教公座，面引應試生員，各給印紙，依式出題考試，不許懷挾代筆，各用印紙，真楷書寫，本學正、錄彌封謄錄，余並依科舉式，助教、博士以次考定。

translations.literal: On the second day of each month at early dawn, after the circular bow, the erudite and assistant erudite of the school sat publicly, personally leading the trial students; each was given sealed paper and topics set according to the form for examination; carrying drafts or ghost-writing was not permitted; each used sealed paper and wrote in regular script; the school's rectifiers and recorders sealed and copied; the remainder followed examination forms; assistant erudite and erudite graded in order.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day of each month at dawn, after the ceremonial bow, erudites and assistants seated themselves and summoned candidates. Each received sealed examination paper, fixed-format questions, no aides or cheat sheets, answers in regular script, copying by rectifiers and recorders, and grading by assistants then erudites according to civil examination practice.

sentences.zh: 次日，監官覆考，於名簿內籍記各得分數，本學收掌，以俟歲終通考。

translations.literal: The next day, supervising officials re-examined, recording each person's score in the name register; the school kept custody to await year-end general examination.
translations.idiomatic: The next day supervisors re-checked papers, logged scores, and the school retained the records until the year-end tally.

sentences.zh: 三曰黜罰科絳。

translations.literal: Third: Demotion, punishment, and disciplinary marks.
translations.idiomatic: Third: demerits, penalties, and expulsion.

sentences.zh: 應私試積分生員，其有不事課業及一切違戾規矩者，初犯罰一分，再犯罰二分，三犯除名，從學正、錄糾舉，正、錄知見而不糾舉者，從本監議罰之。

translations.literal: Students taking private examinations who accumulated points but did not attend to lessons or in any way violated regulations: first offense penalized one point, second offense two points, third offense expulsion—from school rectifier and recorder impeachment; if rectifier and recorder knew and did not impeach, they were penalized by the supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Students in the point system who neglected coursework or broke rules lost one point on the first offense, two on the second, and were expelled on the third, upon report by rectifiers or recorders; officials who failed to report faced penalties from the supervisor.

sentences.zh: 應已補高等生員，其有違戾規矩者，初犯殿試一年，再犯除名，從學正、錄糾舉之，正、錄知見而不糾舉者，亦從本監議罰之。

translations.literal: Superior students already supplemented who violated regulations: first offense deferred trial presentation one year, second offense expulsion—from school rectifier and recorder impeachment; if rectifier and recorder knew and did not impeach, they too were penalized by the supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Advanced students who broke rules were barred from presentation for one year on the first offense and expelled on the second, upon report by rectifiers or recorders, with the same penalty for officials who failed to report.

sentences.zh: 應在學生員，歲終實歷坐齋不滿半歲者，並行除名。

translations.literal: Students in study whose actual residence in a hall at year-end was less than half a year were all expelled.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end any student with less than half a year's actual residence in a hall was expelled.

sentences.zh: 除月假外，其餘告假，並不準算。

translations.literal: Apart from monthly leave, other requested leave was not counted.
translations.idiomatic: Only monthly leave was credited; other absences did not count toward residence.

sentences.zh: 學正、錄歲終通行考校應在學生員，除蒙古、色目別議外，其餘漢人生員三年不能通一經及不肯勤學者，勒令出學。

translations.literal: School rectifiers and recorders at year-end conducted general examination of students in study; apart from Mongols and persons of other colors, who were discussed separately, the rest of Han students who in three years could not master one classic or were unwilling to study diligently were compelled to leave the school.
translations.idiomatic: At year-end rectifiers and recorders reviewed all students. Mongols and persons of other colors were judged separately; Han students who after three years had not mastered one classic or refused diligent study were expelled.

sentences.zh: 其餘責罰，並依舊規。

translations.literal: Other penalties and punishments all followed the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Other penalties followed the previous rules.

sentences.zh: 泰定三年夏六月，更積分而為貢舉，並依世祖舊制。

translations.literal: Third year of Taiding, sixth month of summer, accumulated points were changed back to presentation and examination, all following Emperor Shizu's old system.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer of the third year of Taiding, the point system was replaced with direct presentation and examination under Emperor Shizu's original rules.

sentences.zh: 其貢試之法，從監學所擬，大概與前法略同，而防閑稍加嚴密焉。

translations.literal: The presentation-examination method followed what the school supervisor proposed, in the main slightly the same as the former law, while precautions were somewhat stricter.
translations.idiomatic: The presentation examinations followed proposals from the school supervisor, broadly similar to the earlier rules but with tighter safeguards.

sentences.zh: 其本學正、錄各二員，司樂一員，典籍二員，管勾一員，及侍儀舍人，舊例舉積分生員充之，後以積分既革，於上齋舉年三十以上、學行堪範後學者為正、錄，通曉音律、學業優贍者為司樂，幹局通敏者為典籍、管勾。

translations.literal: The school's rectifiers and recorders, two each; one director of music; two librarians; one registrar; and ceremonial attendants—by old precedent filled from students who accumulated points; after points were abolished, from the upper halls those thirty years and above whose conduct could model later students became rectifiers and recorders; those versed in pitch and with superior learning became director of music; those with capable clerical affairs became librarians and registrars.
translations.idiomatic: The school had two rectifiers, two recorders, one director of music, two librarians, one registrar, and ceremonial attendants. Under the point system these posts went to top students; after points were abolished, rectifiers and recorders were drawn from the upper halls among students over thirty whose conduct could serve as a model; the musically skilled became director of music; capable administrators became librarians and registrars.

sentences.zh: 其侍儀舍人，於上、中齋舉禮儀習熟、音吐洪暢、曾掌春秋釋奠、每月告朔明贊、眾與其能者充之。

translations.literal: Ceremonial attendants were drawn from the upper and middle halls among those skilled in ritual, with resonant speech, who had managed the seasonal Confucian sacrifice, monthly announcement of the new moon, and public rites—selecting those capable.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial attendants were chosen from the upper and middle halls among students skilled in ritual, with clear delivery, who had assisted at the seasonal Confucian sacrifice, monthly new-moon rites, and other public ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 文宗天歷二年春三月，惟伴讀員數，自初二十人歲貢二人，後於大德七年定四十人歲貢六人，至大四年定四十人歲貢四人，延祐四年歲貢八人為淹滯，既額設四十名，宜充部令史者四人、路教授者四人。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong, second year of Tianli, third month of spring: only the companion-reader quota—from the first twenty persons presenting two per year, later in the seventh year of Dade fixed at forty presenting six per year, in the fourth year of Zhide forty presenting four, in the fourth year of Yanyou eight per year causing backlog; since the quota was already forty names, four should fill Secretariat clerks and four circuit instructors.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of spring of the second year of Tianli under Emperor Wenzong, companion-reader quotas were adjusted: originally twenty with two presented yearly, then forty with six under Dade, four under Zhide, and eight under Yanyou causing a backlog. With the quota fixed at forty, four were to fill Secretariat clerkships and four circuit instructor posts.

sentences.zh: 是後，又命所貢生員，每大比選士，與天下士同試於禮部，策於殿廷，又增至備榜而加選擇焉。

translations.literal: Thereafter, presented students at each great comparison selection of scholars were tested together with scholars of the realm at the Ministry of Rites, and questioned by edict in the palace hall; the reserve roster was also increased and further selection applied.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, presented students sat the metropolitan examination with candidates from across the empire at the Ministry of Rites and faced palace interrogation; the reserve roster was expanded and further selection applied.

sentences.zh: 太宗始定中原，即議建學，設科取士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong first fixed the Central Plains, he promptly deliberated establishing schools and setting categories to take scholars.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong first secured the Central Plains, he immediately planned to establish schools and recruit scholars by examination.

sentences.zh: 世祖中統二年，始命置諸路學校官，凡諸生進修者，嚴加訓誨，務使成材，以備選用。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu, second year of Zhongtong, first ordered establishment of school officers in all circuits; all students advancing in study were strictly instructed and admonished, striving to make them accomplished talents for selection and employment.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongtong under Emperor Shizu, school officers were appointed in every circuit, with strict instruction so that advancing students might become qualified talent for official service.

sentences.zh: 至元十九年夏四月，命雲南諸路皆建學以祀先聖。

translations.literal: Nineteenth year of Zhiyuan, fourth month of summer, ordered that all circuits in Yunnan establish schools to sacrifice to the ancient sages.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer of the nineteenth year of Zhiyuan, every circuit in Yunnan was ordered to build schools for sacrifice to the sages.

sentences.zh: 二十三年二月，帝御德興府行宮，詔江南學校舊有學田，復給之以養士。

translations.literal: Twenty-third year, second month, the emperor resided at the Xingxing Palace in Dexing Prefecture and issued an edict restoring former school fields in Jiangnan to support scholars.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twenty-third year, while at the traveling palace in Dexing Prefecture, the emperor ordered that former school lands in Jiangnan be restored to support students.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，令江南諸路學及各縣學內，設立小學，選老成之士教之，或自願招師，或自受家學於父兄者，亦從其便。

translations.literal: Twenty-eighth year, ordered that within Jiangnan circuit schools and each district school elementary schools be established, selecting elderly accomplished persons to teach them; those willing to recruit teachers themselves or who had received family learning from fathers and elder brothers were also permitted as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year elementary schools were ordered within Jiangnan circuit schools and each district school, taught by elderly scholars of accomplishment, or by those who recruited their own teachers or had been educated at home, as they preferred.

sentences.zh: 其他先儒過化之地，名賢經行之所，與好事之家出錢粟贍學者，並立為書院。

translations.literal: Other places where former Confucians transformed the realm, where famous worthies passed in conduct, and households of goodwill that contributed grain and millet to support scholars were also established as academies.
translations.idiomatic: Sites associated with former Confucians, places where renowned scholars had lived, and philanthropists who funded students were also established as academies.

sentences.zh: 凡師儒之命於朝廷者，曰教授，路府上中州置之。

translations.literal: For teachers appointed by the court, they were called instructors, established in circuits, prefectures, and superior and middle subprefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Teachers appointed by the court were called instructors and served in circuits, prefectures, and superior and middle subprefectures.

sentences.zh: 命於禮部及行省及宣慰司者，曰學正、山長、學錄、教諭，路州縣及書院置之。

translations.literal: Those appointed by the Ministry of Rites, regional secretariats, and pacification commissions were called school rectifiers, academy directors, school recorders, and instructors, established in circuit subprefectures, districts, and academies.
translations.idiomatic: Appointments from the Ministry of Rites, regional secretariats, or pacification commissions were school rectifiers, academy directors, school recorders, and instructors, for subprefectures, districts, and academies.

sentences.zh: 路設教授、學正、學錄各一員，散府上中州設教授一員，下州設學正一員，縣設教諭一員，書院設山長一員。

translations.literal: Circuits established one instructor, school rectifier, and school recorder each; scattered prefectures and superior and middle subprefectures one instructor each; inferior subprefectures one school rectifier each; districts one instructor each; academies one academy director each.
translations.idiomatic: Each circuit had one instructor, school rectifier, and school recorder; scattered prefectures and superior and middle subprefectures one instructor each; inferior subprefectures one school rectifier; districts one instructor; academies one academy director.

sentences.zh: 中原州縣學正、山長、學錄、教諭，並受禮部付身。

translations.literal: School rectifiers, academy directors, school recorders, and instructors of Central Plains subprefectures and districts all received appointment documents from the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the Central Plains, subprefecture and district school rectifiers, academy directors, recorders, and instructors all received credentials from the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 各省所屬州縣學正、山長、學錄、教諭，並受行省及宣慰司劄付。

translations.literal: School rectifiers, academy directors, school recorders, and instructors of subprefectures and districts under each province all received documents from the regional secretariat and pacification commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the provinces, the same posts received appointment documents from the regional secretariat or pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 凡路府州書院，設直學以掌錢谷，從郡守及憲府官試補。

translations.literal: For all circuit, prefecture, and subprefecture academies, a direct student was established to manage funds and grain, tested and supplemented by the prefectural magistrate and surveillance commission officials.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit, prefecture, and subprefecture academies each had a direct student to manage finances, appointed after examination by the prefect and surveillance officials.

sentences.zh: 直學考滿，又試所業十篇，升為學錄、教諭。

translations.literal: When the direct student's term was complete, he was again tested on ten compositions of his specialty and promoted to school recorder or instructor.
translations.idiomatic: After completing his term, the direct student submitted ten compositions in his specialty and, upon passing, was promoted to school recorder or instructor.

sentences.zh: 凡正、長、學錄、教諭，或由集賢院及臺憲等官舉充之。

translations.literal: As for rectifiers, directors, school recorders, and instructors, some were filled by nomination from the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, surveillance censors, and other officials.
translations.idiomatic: Rectifiers, academy directors, school recorders, and instructors might be appointed on recommendation from the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, the surveillance apparatus, or other offices.

sentences.zh: 諭、錄歷兩考，升正、長。

translations.literal: Instructors and recorders, after two examinations, were promoted to rectifier and director.
translations.idiomatic: After two rounds of assessment, instructors and recorders were promoted to school rectifier or academy director.

sentences.zh: 正、長一考，升散府上中州教授。

translations.literal: Rectifiers and directors, after one examination, were promoted to instructor in scattered prefectures and superior and middle subprefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After one assessment, rectifiers and directors advanced to instructor in scattered prefectures or superior and middle subprefectures.

sentences.zh: 上中州教授又歷一考，升路教授。

translations.literal: Instructors of superior and middle subprefectures, after again one examination, were promoted to circuit instructor.
translations.idiomatic: After another assessment, subprefecture instructors were promoted to circuit instructor.

sentences.zh: 教授之上，各省設提舉二員，正提舉從五品，副提舉從七品，提舉凡學校之事。

translations.literal: Above instructors, each province established two intendants; the chief intendant was Associate Fifth Rank, the deputy Associate Seventh Rank; intendants oversaw all school affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Each province appointed two school superintendents above the rank of instructor—a chief at associate fifth rank and a deputy at associate seventh rank—charged with all educational administration.

sentences.zh: 後改直學考滿為州吏，例以下第舉人充正、長，備榜舉人充諭、錄，有薦舉者，亦參用之。

translations.literal: Later it was changed that direct students, when examinations were complete, became subprefecture clerks; by rule lower-tier degree holders filled rectifier and director posts, alternate-list examinees filled instructor and recorder posts; when there were nominations, these were also used supplementarily.
translations.idiomatic: Later reforms made direct students who completed their terms into subprefecture clerks. Lower-tier civil examination graduates routinely filled rectifier and director posts, alternate-list graduates served as instructors and recorders, and nominees were also considered.

sentences.zh: 自京學及州縣學以及書院，凡生徒之肄業於是者，守令舉薦之，臺憲考核之，或用為教官，或取為吏屬，往往人材輩出矣。

translations.literal: From the capital school to district and subprefecture schools and academies—for all students pursuing study there—prefects and magistrates recommended them, surveillance offices examined them, and some were used as teaching officials or taken as clerical staff; talent often emerged in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Students at the capital school, local schools, and academies were recommended by magistrates, vetted by the surveillance system, and appointed either as instructors or clerks—yielding a steady stream of talent.

sentences.zh: 世祖中統二年夏五月，太醫院使王猷言：「醫學久廢，後進無所師授。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu, second year of Zhongtong, fifth month of summer, Director of the Imperial Medical Service Wang You said: "Medical learning has long been abandoned; the younger generation has no masters from whom to receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer of the second year of Zhongtong, Wang You, director of the Imperial Medical Service, reported to Emperor Shizu: "Medical education has long lain dormant, and no teachers remain for the young.

sentences.zh: 竊恐朝廷一時取人，學非其傳，為害甚大。」

translations.literal: I privately fear that if the court at one stroke takes people whose learning is not of its proper transmission, the harm would be very great."
translations.idiomatic: I fear that if the court recruits physicians hastily without proper training, the harm will be grave."

sentences.zh: 乃遣副使王安仁授以金牌，往諸路設立醫學。

translations.literal: Thereupon Deputy Commissioner Wang Anren was dispatched, granted a gold tablet, to go to all circuits and establish medical schools.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent Deputy Commissioner Wang Anren with a gold tablet to establish medical schools in every circuit.

sentences.zh: 其生員擬免本身檢醫差占等役，俟其學有所成，每月試以疑難，視其所對優劣，量加勸懲。

translations.literal: Its students were proposed to be exempted from personal medical inspection corvée and requisitioned service; when their learning had achievement, each month they were tested with difficult cases, and according to the superiority or inferiority of their answers, rewards and punishments were applied in measure.
translations.idiomatic: Students were exempted from medical corvée and draft duties. Once they had made progress, monthly examinations on difficult cases determined rewards and discipline according to their performance.

sentences.zh: 後又定醫學之制，設諸路提舉綱維之。

translations.literal: Later the medical school system was again fixed, and circuit intendants were established to oversee and maintain it.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations were later codified and circuit superintendents appointed to oversee medical education.

sentences.zh: 凡宮壸所需，省臺所用，轉入常調，可任親民，其從太醫院自遷轉者，不得視此例，又以示仕途不可以雜進也。

translations.literal: All needed by the palace inner quarters and used by the secretariat and surveillance, upon transfer entered regular quota and could hold posts governing the people; those promoted from within the Imperial Medical Service were not to be viewed under this precedent—also to show that official careers might not advance through mixed channels.
translations.idiomatic: Graduates serving the palace or secretariat could enter the regular civil roster and hold magistracies, but physicians promoted from within the Imperial Medical Service were excluded—a sign that mixed paths must not adulterate the civil service.

sentences.zh: 然太醫院官既受宣命，皆同文武正官五品以上遷敘，余以舊品職遞升，子孫蔭用同正班敘。

translations.literal: Yet Imperial Medical Service officials, once they received imperial commissions, were all alike in promotion with civil and military regular officials of Fifth Rank and above; the rest rose stepwise by former rank and office; descendants enjoyed hereditary privilege with the same roster treatment as regular officials.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the Imperial Medical Service who received imperial commissions were promoted like fifth-rank civil and military officials; others advanced by seniority, and descendants enjoyed hereditary privilege on the regular roster.

sentences.zh: 其掌藥，充都監直長，充禦藥院副使，升至大使，考滿依舊例於流官銓註。

translations.literal: Pharmacy stewards served as chief supervisors and direct chiefs, served as deputy commissioners of the Imperial Pharmacy, rose to commissioner, and when examinations were complete were registered for transitory offices by former precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Pharmacy stewards rose through chief supervisor and direct chief to deputy and then commissioner of the Imperial Pharmacy; upon completing their terms they were assigned transitory posts under the usual rules.

sentences.zh: 諸教授皆從太醫院定擬，而各路主善亦擬同教授皆從九品。

translations.literal: All instructors were nominated and fixed by the Imperial Medical Service, and chief masters of excellence in each circuit were also proposed alike to instructors, all Associate Ninth Rank.
translations.idiomatic: All medical instructors were appointed by the Imperial Medical Service; circuit chief practitioners were proposed at the same rank as instructors—associate ninth.

sentences.zh: 凡隨朝太醫，及醫官子弟，及路府州縣學官，並須試驗。

translations.literal: All court-attending imperial physicians, medical officials' sons and younger brothers, and circuit, prefecture, subprefecture, and district school officials—all must undergo testing.
translations.idiomatic: Court physicians, sons of medical officials, and students at circuit and local medical schools were all subject to examination.

sentences.zh: 其各處名醫所述醫經文字，悉從考校。

translations.literal: Medical classic texts set forth by famous physicians in each place were all subjected to examination and verification.
translations.idiomatic: Medical texts attributed to renowned local physicians were all examined and verified.

sentences.zh: 其諸藥所產性味真偽，悉從辨驗。

translations.literal: The places where the various drugs were produced, their natures, flavors, truth and falsity—all were subjected to discrimination and verification.
translations.idiomatic: The origins, properties, and authenticity of drugs were all inspected.

sentences.zh: 其隨路學校，每歲出降十三科疑難題目，具呈太醫院，發下諸路醫學，令生員依式習課醫義，年終置簿解納送本司，以定其優劣焉。

translations.literal: Their circuit schools each year issued thirteen categories of difficult examination topics, fully presented to the Imperial Medical Service, sent down to circuit medical schools, ordering students according to the form to practice medical principles; at year's end registers were prepared, submitted, and sent to the main office, to determine their superiority and inferiority.
translations.idiomatic: Each year circuit schools received thirteen categories of difficult cases from the Imperial Medical Service. Students studied these cases, and year-end reports sent to the ministry determined their standing.

sentences.zh: 世祖至元二十八年夏六月，始置諸路陰陽學。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu, twenty-eighth year of Zhiyuan, sixth month of summer, first established Yin-Yang schools in all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer of the twenty-eighth year of Zhiyuan, Emperor Shizu first established Yin-Yang schools in every circuit.

sentences.zh: 其在腹裏、江南，若有通曉陰陽之人，各路官司詳加取勘，依儒學、醫學之例，每路設教授以訓誨之。

translations.literal: In the metropolitan core and Jiangnan, if there were persons penetrating yin-yang, each circuit office thoroughly investigated and took them, following the precedents of Confucian and medical schools; each circuit established an instructor to instruct and admonish them.
translations.idiomatic: In the metropolitan region and Jiangnan, those versed in yin-yang lore were vetted by circuit officials. Following the model of Confucian and medical schools, each circuit appointed a professor to instruct them.

sentences.zh: 其有術數精通者，每歲錄呈省府，赴都試驗，果有異能，則於司天臺內許令近侍。

translations.literal: Those penetrating in prognostic arts and numbers, each year were recorded and presented to the provincial government, went to the capital for trial examination; if they truly had extraordinary ability, they were permitted to attend closely within the Astronomical Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Those expert in divination and numerology were each year reported to the provincial authorities and summoned to the capital for examination. The genuinely gifted were allowed to serve at the Astronomical Bureau.

sentences.zh: 延祐初，令陰陽人依儒、醫例，於路府州設教授一員，凡陰陽人皆管轄之，而上屬於太史焉。

translations.literal: Early in Yanyou, yin-yang practitioners were ordered to follow the Confucian and medical precedents: at circuit, prefecture, and subprefecture one instructor was established; all yin-yang practitioners were governed thereby, and above submitted to the Grand Astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yanyou era, yin-yang practitioners were regulated like Confucian and medical students, with one instructor at each circuit, prefecture, and subprefecture, all under the Grand Astrologer.

sentences.zh: 舉遺逸以求隱跡之士，擢茂異以待非常之人。

translations.literal: Recommend the lost and left behind to seek men of hidden traces; elevate the flourishing and exceptional to await extraordinary persons.
translations.idiomatic: The court sought recluses by summoning the neglected, and elevated exceptional talent to await men of uncommon ability.

sentences.zh: 世祖中統間，征許衡，授懷孟路教官，詔於懷孟等處選子弟之俊秀者教育之。

translations.literal: During Emperor Shizu's Zhongtong period, Xu Heng was summoned, appointed instructor of Huaimeng Circuit, and an edict ordered that in Huaimeng and other places outstanding sons and younger brothers be selected and educated.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhongtong era, Xu Heng was summoned and made instructor for Huaimeng Circuit, with orders to educate gifted youths from that region.

sentences.zh: 是年，又詔征金進士李冶，授翰林學士。

translations.literal: That year, an edict also summoned Jin dynasty advanced scholar Li Ye and appointed Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Li Ye, a Jin advanced scholar, was summoned and made Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 征劉因為集賢學士，不至。

translations.literal: Liu Yin was summoned as Academician of Scholarly Worthies; he did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin was summoned as Academician of Scholarly Worthies but declined to come.

sentences.zh: 又用平章咸寧王野仙薦，征蕭不起，即授陜西儒學提舉。

translations.literal: Again, on the recommendation of Grand Councilor and Prince of Xianning Yexian, Xiao Ji was summoned but did not rise; he was at once appointed Confucian school intendant of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: On the recommendation of Grand Councilor Yexian, Prince of Xianning, Xiao Ji was summoned but refused; he was nevertheless appointed superintendent of Confucian schools in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 至元十八年，詔求前代聖賢之後，儒醫卜筮，通曉天文歷數，並山林隱逸之士。

translations.literal: Eighteenth year of Zhiyuan, an edict sought descendants of former dynasties' sages and worthies, Confucians, physicians, diviners, and those penetrating astronomy and the calendar, together with recluses in mountains and forests.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Zhiyuan, the throne called for descendants of ancient sages, scholars, physicians, diviners, experts in astronomy and calendrics, and recluses in mountain retreats.

sentences.zh: 二十年，復召拜劉因右贊善大夫，辭，不允。

translations.literal: Twentieth year, Liu Yin was again summoned and appointed Right Assistant in the Palace; he declined and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Liu Yin was again offered the post of Right Assistant in the Palace; he declined, and the court would not accept his refusal.

sentences.zh: 未幾以親老，乞終養，俸給一無所受。

translations.literal: Before long, on account of aged parents, he begged lifelong nurturing care; salary provisions he entirely did not receive.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he pleaded to retire and care for his aged parents, accepting no salary at all.

sentences.zh: 後遣使授命於家，辭疾不起。

translations.literal: Later envoys were sent to grant appointment at his home; he declined on grounds of illness and did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Later envoys brought appointment to his home; citing illness, he still refused to serve.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，復詔求隱晦之士，俾有司具以名聞。

translations.literal: Twenty-eighth year, again an edict sought obscure gentlemen, ordering responsible offices to prepare and report their names.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year another edict sought hidden worthies, requiring local officials to submit their names.

sentences.zh: 成宗大德六年，征臨川布衣吳澂，擢應奉翰林文字，拜命即歸。

translations.literal: Emperor Chengzong, sixth year of Dade, summoned Linchuan commoner Wu Cheng, elevated to Attendant of the Hanlin Script, accepted appointment and immediately returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Dade, Wu Cheng, a commoner from Linchuan, was summoned and made Attendant of Hanlin Script; he accepted the post and at once went home.

sentences.zh: 九年，詔求山林間有德行文學、識治道者，遣使征蕭渼，且曰：「或不樂於仕，可試一來，與朕語而遣歸。」

translations.literal: Ninth year, an edict sought among mountains and forests those with virtue and conduct, literary cultivation, and penetrating governance—envoys were sent to summon Xiao Rang, and it was said: "Or if you do not delight in office, you may try coming once, speak with Us and be sent home."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the throne sought virtuous and learned men in mountain retreats who understood government, and sent envoys to summon Xiao Rang with this message: "If office holds no appeal, come once to speak with Us, and you may go home."

sentences.zh: 至大三年，復召吳澄，拜國子司業，以病還；

translations.literal: Third year of Zhida, Wu Cheng was again summoned, appointed Directorate Vice Commissioner, returned on account of illness;
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhida, Wu Cheng was again summoned as Vice Commissioner of the Directorate but returned ill;

sentences.zh: 延祐三年，召拜集賢直學士，以疾不赴；

translations.literal: Third year of Yanyou, summoned and appointed Direct Academician of Scholarly Worthies, did not go on account of illness;
translations.idiomatic: in the third year of Yanyou he was made Direct Academician of Scholarly Worthies but did not attend owing to illness;

sentences.zh: 至治三年，召拜翰林學士。

translations.literal: Third year of Zhizhi, summoned and appointed Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: in the third year of Zhizhi he was appointed Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 武宗、仁宗累征蕭渼，授集賢學士、國子司業，未赴，改集賢侍講學士。

translations.literal: Emperors Wuzong and Renzong repeatedly summoned Xiao Rang, appointed Academician of Scholarly Worthies and Directorate Vice Commissioner; he did not go, and was changed to Attendant Lecturer of Scholarly Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Wuzong and Renzong summoned Xiao Rang repeatedly, offering him posts as Academician and Directorate Vice Commissioner; he declined, and the offer was changed to Attendant Lecturer of Scholarly Worthies.

sentences.zh: 又以太子右諭德征，始至京師，授集賢學士、國子祭酒，諭德如故。

translations.literal: Again he was summoned as Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent; only then did he reach the capital, appointed Academician of Scholarly Worthies and Directorate Rector, mentor as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned again as Right Mentor to the Heir Apparent and only then came to the capital, receiving joint appointment as Academician and Directorate Rector while retaining his mentor title.

sentences.zh: 仁宗延祐七年十一月，詔曰：「比歲設立科舉，以取人材，尚慮高尚之士，晦跡丘園，無從可致。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong, seventh year of Yanyou, eleventh month, edict said: "In recent years civil examinations have been established to obtain human talent; we still fear that lofty gentlemen, hiding their traces in garden mounds, have no means by which to be brought forth.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the seventh year of Yanyou, Emperor Renzong issued an edict: "Civil examinations have lately been instituted to recruit talent, yet we fear that eminent men dwelling in obscurity among hills and gardens cannot be reached.

sentences.zh: 各處其有隱居行義、才德高邁、深明治道、不求聞達者，所在官司具姓名，牒報本道廉訪司，覆奏察聞，以備錄用。」

translations.literal: Wherever there are those dwelling in seclusion practicing righteousness, talent and virtue lofty and far-reaching, deeply penetrating governing principles and not seeking renown, the local office in each place shall prepare their names, memorialize and report to the circuit surveillance commission of the original circuit, re-present for examination and report, to prepare for record and employment."
translations.idiomatic: Wherever men of moral excellence live in seclusion, possess lofty talent and virtue, understand government deeply, and seek no fame, local offices shall report their names to the circuit surveillance commission for review and possible appointment."

sentences.zh: 又屢詔求言於下，使得進言於上，雖指斥時政，並無譴責，往往采擇其言，任用其人，列諸庶位，以圖治功。

translations.literal: Again and again edicts sought words from below, enabling speech to advance to above; even when pointing out and blaming current government, altogether there was no rebuke and punishment; often their words were selected and adopted, and the persons employed, arrayed among various posts, to plan governing achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated edicts also invited criticism from below. Even denunciations of current policy went unpunished. The court often adopted such counsel and appointed the speakers to various posts in pursuit of good government.

sentences.zh: 其他著書立言、裨益教化、啟迪後人者，亦斟酌錄用，著為常式云。

translations.literal: Others who wrote books and established words, benefiting teaching and transformation and opening and enlightening later people, were also weighed and considered for record and employment, established as a constant form—thus.
translations.idiomatic: Authors whose writings enriched education and enlightened posterity were also considered for appointment, and this became standing practice.

sentences.zh: 童子舉，唐、宋始著於科，然亦無常員。

translations.literal: Presentation of child prodigies: Tang and Song first entered it in the examination categories, yet there were also no fixed quotas.
translations.idiomatic: The presentation of child prodigies first appeared in Tang and Song examinations but had no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 成宗大德三年，舉童子楊山童、海童。

translations.literal: Emperor Chengzong, third year of Dade, presented child prodigies Yang Shantong and Haitong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dade under Emperor Chengzong, the prodigies Yang Shantong and Haitong were presented.

sentences.zh: 五年，大都提舉學校所舉安西路張秦山，江浙行省舉張升甫。

translations.literal: Fifth year, the Daidu school intendant's office presented Anxi Circuit's Zhang Qinshan; the Jiangzhe regional secretariat presented Zhang Shengfu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the Daidu school superintendent presented Zhang Qinshan of Anxi Circuit, and the Jiangzhe regional secretariat presented Zhang Shengfu.

sentences.zh: 武宗至大元年，舉武福安。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong, first year of Zhida, presented Wu Fu'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhida under Emperor Wuzong, Wu Fu'an was presented.

sentences.zh: 仁宗延祐三年，江浙行省舉俞傅孫、馮怙哥。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong, third year of Yanyou, the Jiangzhe regional secretariat presented Yu Fusun and Feng Hugge.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yanyou the Jiangzhe regional secretariat presented Yu Fusun and Feng Hugge.

sentences.zh: 六年，河南路舉張答罕，學士完者不花舉丁頑頑。

translations.literal: Sixth year, Henan Circuit presented Zhang Dahan; Academician Wan Zhebuhua presented Ding Wanwan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Henan Circuit presented Zhang Dahan, and Academician Wan Zhebuhua presented Ding Wanwan.

sentences.zh: 七年，河間縣舉杜山童，大興縣舉陳聃。

translations.literal: Seventh year, Hejian District presented Du Shantong; Daxing District presented Chen Dan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Hejian District presented Du Shantong and Daxing District presented Chen Dan.

sentences.zh: 英宗至治元年，福州路連江縣舉陳元麟。

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong, first year of Zhizhi, Fuzhou Circuit Lianjiang District presented Chen Yuanlin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhizhi under Emperor Yingzong, Lianjiang District in Fuzhou Circuit presented Chen Yuanlin.

sentences.zh: 至治三年，河南行省舉張英。

translations.literal: Third year of Zhizhi, Henan regional secretariat presented Zhang Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhizhi the Henan regional secretariat presented Zhang Ying.

sentences.zh: 泰定四年，福州舉葉留井。

translations.literal: Fourth year of Taiding, Fuzhou presented Ye Liujing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taiding, Fuzhou presented Ye Liujing.

sentences.zh: 文宗天歷二年，舉杜夙靈。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong, second year of Tianli, presented Du Suling.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianli under Emperor Wenzong, Du Suling was presented.

sentences.zh: 至順二年，制舉答不歹子買來的。

translations.literal: Second year of Zhishun, special presentation of Dabutai's son Mailaide.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhishun, Mailaide, son of Dabutai, was presented by special decree.

sentences.zh: 皆以其天資穎悟，超出兒輩，或能默誦經文，書寫大字，或能綴緝辭章，講說經史，並令入國子學教育之。

translations.literal: All because their inborn nature was sharp and penetrating, surpassing their child cohort, or could silently recite classic texts and write large characters, or could stitch together literary compositions and lecture on classics and histories—all were ordered to enter the Directorate of Learning to be educated.
translations.idiomatic: All were admitted to the Directorate of Learning because their native gifts far outstripped their peers—some could recite classics from memory or write large characters, others compose essays or expound on the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 惟張秦山尤精篆涘，陳元麟能通性理，葉留井問以《四書》大義，則對曰：「無過事父母能竭其力，事君能致其身。」

translations.literal: Only Zhang Qinshan was especially penetrating in seal script; Chen Yuanlin could penetrate nature and principle; Ye Liujing was asked the great meaning of the Four Books and replied: "Nothing surpasses serving parents and being able to exhaust one's strength, serving the ruler and being able to give one's body."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qinshan excelled especially in seal script; Chen Yuanlin had mastered Neo-Confucian principle; when Ye Liujing was questioned on the Four Books, he answered: "Nothing surpasses serving one's parents with all one's strength and serving one's ruler with one's life."

sentences.zh: 時人以遠大期之。

translations.literal: People of the time expected great things from afar for him.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries looked to him for great things ahead.
